# Accessibility QA

Combine automated rules with manual interaction. An axe scan alone never proves WCAG conformance.

## Hard gates

1. Resolve target pages, critical user journeys, WCAG level, browsers, viewport, language, authentication, and assistive technology scope
2. Read the project app guide and matching feature guide before browser interaction when working inside QA-MDS
3. Write a test contract with target, role, journey, expected behavior, evidence path, and stop condition
4. Run automated checks only after the relevant dynamic state is visible
5. Verify keyboard and focus behavior manually for every critical journey
6. Keep automated violations, incomplete checks, and manual findings separate
7. Never claim a screen reader passed unless that screen reader and browser combination was actually exercised

Read [references/MANUAL_MATRIX.md](references/MANUAL_MATRIX.md) before a full audit.

## Tool routing

- Use Playwright CLI or the existing `qa-run` browser route to reach deterministic states
- Use `@axe-core/playwright` for WCAG-tagged automated checks; start from [assets/axe-playwright.spec.ts](assets/axe-playwright.spec.ts)
- Use Playwright MCP only for an unfamiliar interactive branch that cannot be understood efficiently through scoped CLI snapshots
- Use browser-native accessibility inspection for name, role, state, and relationships
- Use BrowserStack only when licensed real-browser, real-device, or its accessibility service is required
- Use a real screen reader for screen-reader verdicts: VoiceOver on macOS/iOS, NVDA or JAWS on Windows, TalkBack on Android

## Workflow

### 1. Inventory journeys and states

List critical pages and expose default, loading, error, empty, validation, modal, menu, expanded, notification, and success states. Include logged-out and role-specific states where applicable.

### 2. Run automated checks

Run axe at page load and again after opening dynamic content. Store the rule ID, WCAG tags, impact, target selector, help URL, and page state. Do not paste full DOM or accessibility trees into reports.

### 3. Run keyboard checks

Starting with no pointer interaction, verify skip links, tab order, visible focus, reverse navigation, activation, escape behavior, focus trap, return focus, no keyboard trap, and access to every critical action.

### 4. Verify semantics and forms

Check landmarks, headings, accessible names, roles, states, instructions, labels, required fields, error identification, error association, status announcements, table semantics, and alternative text.

### 5. Verify visual adaptation

Check 200% zoom, 400% where applicable, 320 CSS-pixel reflow, text spacing, orientation, contrast, non-text contrast, target size, motion, flashing, and content on hover or focus.

### 6. Run screen-reader journeys

Exercise only the agreed critical paths. Record screen reader, browser, OS, version, reading order, announcements, control name and state, errors, live regions, and blocker details.

### 7. Report and retest

Group duplicate nodes by root cause. Each finding includes WCAG criterion, affected journey, steps, actual announcement or behavior, expected behavior, impact on users, evidence, severity, and remediation direction.

## Completion checks

- Automated scans covered visible dynamic states
- Incomplete axe results were manually reviewed or marked blocked
- Keyboard-only critical journeys have verdicts
- Focus entry, trap, escape, and return were checked for overlays
- Zoom and reflow were checked
- Screen-reader claims name the actual environment
- Findings identify user impact and WCAG criterion
- Coverage gaps remain explicit

# AI Quality QA

Evaluate behavior statistically and case-by-case. Do not judge an AI feature from a few conversational examples.

## Hard gates

1. Resolve feature, model or prompt version, environment, dataset, expected behavior, allowed tools, safety policy, and budget
2. Freeze a versioned evaluation dataset before comparing candidates
3. Keep secrets, personal data, hidden prompts, and credentials out of evaluation artifacts
4. Separate deterministic assertions, rubric judgments, safety checks, and human review
5. Use the same dataset and evaluator configuration for comparisons
6. Never mark hallucination, grounding, or safety as passed from exact-match rate alone
7. Record model, prompt, retrieval, tool, temperature, seed when supported, latency, token use, and cost

Read [references/EVALUATION_MATRIX.md](references/EVALUATION_MATRIX.md) when choosing metrics and coverage.

## Workflow

### 1. Define the contract

Record:

- User intent and supported use cases
- Allowed and forbidden behavior
- Required sources or grounding
- Expected output schema
- Tool permissions and side effects
- Language and locale
- Quality, latency, reliability, and cost thresholds
- Escalation and refusal behavior

### 2. Build a versioned dataset

Include happy paths, boundary inputs, ambiguous requests, missing context, multilingual inputs, prompt injection, sensitive data, unavailable tools, tool errors, long context, and known regressions. Give every case a stable ID and source.

Split datasets into development and holdout sets. Do not tune prompts directly against the final holdout set.

### 3. Select evaluators

- Use deterministic code for JSON validity, schema, required fields, citations, tool name, arguments, forbidden terms, latency, and cost
- Use reference matching only where wording is genuinely deterministic
- Use rubric-based model judgment for relevance or tone, with a written rubric and periodic human calibration
- Use human review for high-impact safety, nuanced grounding, or disagreements between evaluators

For JSONL datasets with deterministic expectations:

```bash
python3 scripts/evaluate_jsonl.py cases.jsonl \
  --min-pass-rate 0.95 \
  --max-p95-latency-ms 5000 \
  --output evidence/ai-eval.json
```

### 4. Run and trace

Capture one record per case containing input ID, configuration version, output, retrieved source IDs, tool calls, latency, tokens, cost, evaluator results, and redacted trace reference. Do not store raw secrets or unrestricted personal data.

### 5. Analyze failures

Classify failures as prompt, retrieval, context, tool selection, tool arguments, model reasoning, structured output, policy, latency, cost, infrastructure, or evaluator ambiguity. Reproduce with the same configuration and compare a control case.

### 6. Compare candidates

Report paired results by case, not only aggregate averages. A candidate passes only when required quality and safety thresholds hold and no critical regression is hidden by a higher average score.

### 7. Report

Include dataset version, configuration versions, thresholds, aggregate metrics, failed case IDs, severity, trace references, cost, latency distribution, known evaluator limitations, and coverage gaps.

## Completion checks

- Dataset and configuration are versioned
- Holdout cases were not used for prompt tuning
- Deterministic and subjective evaluators are separated
- Grounding and tool calls have direct evidence
- Safety-critical failures are reviewed individually
- Latency and cost include p95 or another agreed percentile
- Candidate comparison uses the same cases
- Failed and blocked cases remain visible

# API Contract QA

Verify both the specification and the observable implementation. A valid OpenAPI document does not prove the API follows it.

## Hard gates

1. Resolve specification version, target environment, base URL, authentication, roles, allowed mutations, rate limit, test data, and cleanup
2. Treat the supplied specification as proposed behavior when requirements are unconfirmed; do not invent missing expected status or schema
3. Use least-privilege test credentials and never print tokens or secret headers
4. Run static validation before live requests
5. Separate documentation defects, implementation defects, environment blockers, and backward-compatibility risks
6. Verify response semantics and business outcome, not only HTTP 2xx
7. Clean up every created resource and verify deletion or rollback

Read [references/CONTRACT_MATRIX.md](references/CONTRACT_MATRIX.md) when designing endpoint coverage.

Route Postman MCP installation, authentication, diagnosis, and workspace operations to `postman`. Read [references/POSTMAN_MCP.md](references/POSTMAN_MCP.md) when the Postman connection affects contract execution. Run `../github-mcp-qa/scripts/doctor-stack.sh postman` after configuration.

## Tool routing

- Run `scripts/check_openapi.py` for a deterministic OpenAPI 3 structural preflight
- Use project-native Playwright API tests or start from [assets/api-contract.spec.ts](assets/api-contract.spec.ts) for stable regression
- Use Postman MCP for workspace, collection, specification, mock, and monitor management; execute collections through `postman/scripts/runner.py`
- Use Schemathesis or another schema-driven runner only when installed and approved by the project
- Use `testcase-template` when the user asks to produce testcase Markdown or Excel; keep execution in this skill
- Route performance behavior, JMeter and k6 work to the single public `performance-qa`
- Route exploit-focused authorization testing to `pentest-run`

## Workflow

### 1. Import and preflight

Record the source file and checksum. Validate syntax, OpenAPI version, paths, methods, operation IDs, parameters, responses, local references, server variables, and security definitions.

```bash
python3 scripts/check_openapi.py openapi.json --output evidence/openapi-preflight.json
```

### 2. Build the operation ledger

For every in-scope operation record method, path, auth role, parameters, request variants, success responses, error responses, side effects, cleanup, and coverage status.

### 3. Verify live behavior

Cover valid, missing, null, malformed, boundary, unexpected, unauthorized, forbidden, not found, conflict, rate-limit, and unsupported media-type cases when specified or confirmed. Validate status, headers, content type, schema, field semantics, and persisted side effects.

### 4. Verify cross-operation rules

Check create-read-update-delete lifecycle, idempotency keys, retry behavior, pagination boundaries, filtering, sorting, concurrency controls such as ETag, webhook signature and retry, version negotiation, and error shape consistency where applicable.

### 5. Review compatibility

Compare the candidate specification with the released baseline. Flag removed paths or methods, new required input, removed enum values, narrowed types, changed defaults, changed auth, incompatible response changes, and semantic changes. Do not label additive optional fields as breaking without a consumer constraint.

### 6. Report

Each mismatch includes operation ID, method and path, role, request case, specification expectation, actual status or schema, business impact, redacted request and response evidence, cleanup status, and classification.

## Completion checks

- Specification source and version are identified
- Static errors are resolved or reported
- Every operation has coverage status
- Required success and error responses were exercised or blocked
- Authentication and authorization roles are explicit
- Pagination, idempotency, and lifecycle rules have verdicts when applicable
- Backward-compatibility risks are separate from runtime defects
- Mutated data is cleaned up

name: business-analysis
description: Analyze BRD, SRS, FRS, requirements, and system documents as a senior fullstack QA/QC tester after local non-Markdown sources pass through doc-to-md. Trigger on business flow, requirement analysis, editable XMind map, prerequisites, related functions, ambiguity or gap analysis, clarification questions, Q&A Markdown, or Q&A Excel; do not require the skill name. For Drive URLs, use google-drive-qa to access the source first. Produce the Vietnamese XMind and matching Q&A deliverables from one validated JSON source before testcase design or browser testing
---

# Business Analysis

Convert first, reason once, render deterministically

## Hard gates

0. **Before reading the BRD/SRS, check the knowledge base from REPO_BUSINESS_DISCOVERY:**
   - Check `qa-knowledge/merged/system-business-guide.md` — if it exists, read it first to understand the system architecture
   - Check `qa-knowledge/merged/system-qna.json` — if it exists, load the confirmed Q&A, do not create duplicates
   - Check `qa-knowledge/repositories/<repo>/reconciliation-report.json` — prioritize entries with `result: CONFIRMED`; clearly highlight `CONFLICT`s, do not blindly choose one source
   - Check `qa-knowledge/repositories/<repo>/business-qna.json` — merge existing Q&A, only generate new Q&A for uncovered areas
   - Check `qa-knowledge/repositories/<repo>/runtime-findings.json` — if it exists, read it first to acknowledge runtime confirmed security/permission CONFLICTs without creating duplicate Q&A
   - Check `qa-knowledge/repositories/<repo>/graphify-discovery.json` — if it exists, use dependency candidates to find related functions and missing cross-flow questions; never promote a Graphify relation to `verified`
   - If source and doc contradict: record both, mark as `conflict`, and require human confirmation
   - If no knowledge files are found: proceed normally from gate 1

1. Resolve the exact source documents and project output folder
2. For PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML or image input, run `doc-to-md/scripts/convert.sh` first
3. Read the converted Markdown, not the binary document, and preserve source heading or requirement references
4. Review all 18 areas in [references/SENIOR_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md](references/SENIOR_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md)
5. Build one structured JSON using [references/INPUT_SCHEMA.md](references/INPUT_SCHEMA.md) and keep its human-readable content in Vietnamese
6. Define entry state, exit state, required business outcomes and explicit cross-flow links for every system flow
7. Build at least one end-to-end path in the internal `sanity_journeys` field with preparation conditions, ordered functions, transition conditions, business control points and final results
8. Never turn an observed behavior or inference into a confirmed business rule
9. Run `scripts/generate.sh` to create XMind and both Q&A formats
10. Validate and read back the generated Markdown, Excel IDs and XMind package before reporting success

Do not write testcases in this skill. Hand the confirmed Markdown and Q&A answers to `testcase-template` later

## Workflow

### 1. Convert the source

If the source is not Markdown:

```bash
bash <doc-to-md>/scripts/convert.sh <source-file> <project-output>/<source-stem>.md
```

Keep the Markdown beside the analysis outputs so future AI can reread it without parsing the original binary

### 2. Extract the business model

Record only what the source supports:

- Scope, actors and permissions
- Module and entry point
- Preconditions and trigger
- Happy, alternate and exception flows
- State transitions and persistence
- Business rules, input validation and calculations
- Side effects, API, data and third-party integration
- UI/UX, accessibility and non-functional expectations
- Acceptance criteria and testability

For every flow, also record:

- Entry state and exit state
- Preconditions that must be prepared before executing the business flow
- Ordered system processing steps and state changes
- Minimum business outcomes that prove the flow completed correctly
- Upstream and downstream functions through top-level `flow_links`
- End-to-end execution paths through the internal `sanity_journeys` field

Mark each fact `verified`, `inferred` or `unresolved` with a source reference

### 3. Perform senior QA/QC review

Read [references/SENIOR_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md](references/SENIOR_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md) completely

For every review area, set exactly one status:

- `checked` when the document is clear enough or questions were created
- `blocked` when the source, role or context is missing
- `not_applicable` only with a reason

Create Q&A for ambiguity, contradiction, missing rule, untestable expectation, unsafe assumption or unclear ownership. Keep proposed assumptions separate from confirmed answers

### 4. Save the structured source

Save the machine source inside a hidden technical folder:

```text
<project-output>/.business-analysis/<project-name>_Analysis_Source.json
```

This JSON is not a user deliverable. It is the internal source that keeps IDs and content synchronized across Markdown, Excel and XMind. Update the JSON and regenerate instead of editing those three outputs independently

### 5. Generate all outputs

```bash
bash scripts/generate.sh \
  .business-analysis/<project-name>_Analysis_Source.json \
  <project-output> \
  <project-name>
```

Outputs:

```text
<project-name>_Business_Flow.xmind
<project-name>_Q&A.md
<project-name>_Q&A.xlsx
```

The XMind file is generated with the official `xmindmark` package and remains editable in XMind

The XMind is a business and system flow map, not a document dump or test report. It must show the end-to-end system sequence, prerequisites, entry and exit states, required business outcomes, related functions and real relationship arrows between linked flows. Keep detailed Q&A and review coverage in Markdown and Excel only

The XMind must use exactly one `Luồng hệ thống` sheet so readers see the end-to-end journey and its functions on the same canvas. Render each internal journey path as a horizontal lane under the shared root. Every lane step is the real system function, not a separate summary node. Keep prerequisites, states, business control points, required outcomes and related functions folded under that same function node

### 6. Read back

- Open Q&A Markdown and verify question count, priority and nontechnical readability
- Open Excel and verify the same Question IDs and content
- Run `node scripts/render-xmind.mjs --check <file.xmind> <analysis.json>` and verify journey and relationship counts
- Report `BLOCKED` when conversion, review coverage, dependency or output validation fails

### 7. Optional interactive companion

Only when the user requests HTML, an interactive flow or a visual companion, read [Graphify and effective HTML integration](../qa-run/references/GRAPHIFY-EFFECTIVE-HTML.md), then render from the already validated hidden JSON:

```bash
node ../qa-run/scripts/writers/render-intelligence-html.mjs \
  --input .business-analysis/<project-name>_Analysis_Source.json \
  --output <project-output>/<project-name>_Business_Flow.html

node ../qa-run/scripts/writers/render-intelligence-html.mjs \
  --check <project-output>/<project-name>_Business_Flow.html
```

This HTML is optional and derived. The required `.xmind`, Q&A Markdown and Q&A Excel remain the canonical synchronized deliverables

## Output rules

- Q&A Markdown and Excel must have matching Question IDs and content
- All user-facing headings, descriptions, questions, assumptions and workbook labels must be Vietnamese
- Keep filenames in English using exactly `<project-name>_Business_Flow.xmind`, `<project-name>_Q&A.md` and `<project-name>_Q&A.xlsx`
- Use a restrained navy, teal, blue, amber, red and green palette with readable contrast
- Keep the internal JSON under `.business-analysis` and do not present it as a deliverable
- Keep document paths, section codes, `source_ref` and missing-source diagnostics only in the hidden JSON, never in user-facing Markdown, Excel or XMind
- Use plain business language so a nontechnical reader can understand every visible field
- Keep XMind focused on business flow and connected system behavior, not testing terminology, the complete Q&A or the 18-area review log
- Every XMind flow must show prerequisites, entry state, ordered processing, exit state, required business outcomes and related functions
- Render every item in `flow_links` as a visible function-to-function section and a real XMind relationship arrow
- Create exactly one `Luồng hệ thống` sheet containing every business journey and every function
- Render each internal `sanity_journeys` path as a horizontal business lane on the shared canvas
- Show preparation conditions, every ordered function and final result in the same lane
- Put transition conditions, business control points, entry and exit states, prerequisites, required outcomes and related functions under the matching function node
- Fold function detail branches by default so the connected flow remains compact and readable
- Render both journey transitions and every `flow_links` item as real relationship arrows on the same sheet
- Never move function relationships or detailed function context to separate sheets
- Keep the legacy JSON keys `sanity_journeys` and `sanity_checks` internal only and never render those names, `SANITY-*` IDs or testing terms in XMind
- Keep unanswered questions `Open` with an empty Answer
- Use `Answered` only when an authority supplied the answer
- Do not use emoji or icons
- Do not end human-readable cells or list items with `.`
- Preserve IDs, URLs, filenames, formulas, decimals, API fields and code exactly
- Do not store passwords, tokens, cookies, API keys or personal sensitive data

## Resources

- [references/INPUT_SCHEMA.md](references/INPUT_SCHEMA.md) for the analysis JSON contract
- [references/SENIOR_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md](references/SENIOR_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md) for the fullstack QA/QC review
- [scripts/generate.sh](scripts/generate.sh) for the complete renderer pipeline
- [scripts/render-qa.py](scripts/render-qa.py) for matching Markdown and Excel Q&A
- [scripts/render-xmind.mjs](scripts/render-xmind.mjs) for editable XMind output
- [examples/sample-analysis.json](examples/sample-analysis.json) for a cross-model example
- [Graphify and effective HTML integration](../qa-run/references/GRAPHIFY-EFFECTIVE-HTML.md) for optional source graph candidates and interactive HTML companions

# Data Quality QA

Run evidence-led data validation without modifying production data.

## Hard gates

1. Resolve source, target, environment, dataset scope, business key, expected transformation, freshness window, and allowed write behavior
2. Write a contract with `Target`, `Operation`, `Required inputs`, `Write action`, and `Verification`
3. Use read-only credentials by default and never print connection strings, passwords, tokens, or raw personal data
4. Capture the pre-run row count, schema, partition or watermark, and test-data ownership
5. Separate source defects, pipeline defects, target defects, and environment blockers
6. Never call a dataset correct from row count alone
7. Clean up only records created by the run and verify the cleanup

## Tool routing

- Use `scripts/reconcile_csv.py` for deterministic CSV source-to-target comparison
- Use read-only SQL for database validation; prefer aggregate evidence and redacted samples
- Use Great Expectations when a project already uses it or needs reusable expectation suites
- Use dbt tests or dbt MCP only when dbt is actually present; start with discovery and compile/read operations before commands that can materialize data
- Use project-native Spark/Delta tools for OneBrain rather than introducing dbt only for QA
- Use browser QA only to trigger or observe a pipeline; validate persisted data through the data layer

Read [references/DATABASE_MCP.md](references/DATABASE_MCP.md) before configuring any database MCP. Never accept a normal application account as proof of read-only access. Run `../github-mcp-qa/scripts/doctor-stack.sh database-readonly` after configuration.

Read [references/CHECK_MATRIX.md](references/CHECK_MATRIX.md) when designing coverage or reconciling an ingestion flow.

## Workflow

### 1. Map the data flow

Record source, ingestion or transform stages, target, business key, partition key, watermark, retry behavior, and observable side effects. Mark unknown logic as `Open`; do not convert an inference into an expected rule.

### 2. Build a coverage ledger

Include applicable checks for:

- Schema and type fidelity
- Completeness and row reconciliation
- Accuracy and transformation rules
- Uniqueness and duplicate handling
- Null and default semantics
- Referential integrity
- Freshness and late-arriving data
- Incremental load, replay, retry, and idempotency
- Precision, timezone, Unicode, encoding, and boundary values
- Lineage from source field to target field
- Permissions, tenant isolation, masking, and retention

Use `covered`, `partial`, `blocked`, or `not_covered` for every applicable area.

### 3. Establish a baseline

Capture source and target schemas, counts, min/max business keys, aggregate totals, null counts, duplicate counts, and current watermark. Prefer queries that cannot mutate state.

### 4. Validate deterministic cases

Use controlled records covering happy path, nulls, duplicates, invalid types, boundary values, Unicode, timestamps, decimal precision, updates, deletes, and late arrivals. Tag every created record with a run-specific key when the system supports it.

For exported CSV datasets:

```bash
python3 scripts/reconcile_csv.py \
  --source source.csv \
  --target target.csv \
  --key id \
  --ignore-columns updated_at \
  --output evidence/reconciliation.json
```

### 5. Validate operational behavior

Verify retry, partial failure, rollback or compensation, persistence after reload, concurrent execution where authorized, and alert or status behavior. State-changing or high-volume tests require explicit approval and a rollback plan.

### 6. Report

For each discrepancy record:

- Check ID and business rule
- Source observation and target observation
- Expected transformation
- Scope and affected rows
- Redacted deterministic evidence
- Suspected layer and confidence
- Severity and cleanup status

Keep `Candidate` until the discrepancy reproduces and a control record behaves correctly.

## Completion checks

- Source and target scope are exact
- Business keys and comparison columns are explicit
- Counts are backed by field-level or aggregate checks
- Schema drift and null semantics were checked
- Incremental and idempotent behavior has a verdict or blocker
- Evidence is redacted
- Test data cleanup is verified
- Coverage gaps remain visible

---
name: doc-to-md
description: Convert local or chat-uploaded PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, image, audio, CSV, JSON, XML, or ZIP files to Markdown for other QA skills. Trigger when the user provides one of these local artifacts and asks to read, extract, convert, or analyze it; do not require the skill name. Use only for an existing local path or upload. Route drive.google.com/docs.google.com URLs and Drive IDs to google-drive-qa unless the user explicitly requests a local export first. Not for editing Markdown or scraping web pages.
---

# Doc to MD

**Core principle:** Only convert local files with correct structure — do not retype manually from PDFs and do not pull Drive sources locally just to convert them.

Uses Microsoft's **MarkItDown** (open-source MIT) to convert PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, images (JPG/PNG with OCR) to Markdown. Files are processed 100% locally (privacy), no cloud uploads. **API key**: NO key required for MarkItDown.

> **When to use**: User uploads a document file (.pdf, .docx, .pptx, .xlsx, .html, .jpg, .png) and wants the AI to read its content.
> **Purpose**: Raw PDF/DOCX files are hard for AI to parse directly. Convert to Markdown first → AI reads MD much easier and understands deeper context.

## Source boundary

1. Require a real local filesystem path before running `convert.sh`.
2. Treat a chat-uploaded file materialized as a local path as local input.
3. Treat a Google Drive URL, Drive ID, Google Docs URL, Google Sheets URL, Google Slides URL, or object resolved through Drive MCP as a remote Drive source.
4. For a remote Drive source, stop this skill and route the request to `google-drive-qa`; consume the in-place MCP content directly.
5. Do not download, export, or copy a Drive source locally merely to make it eligible for this skill.
6. Allow conversion after a Drive download or export only when the user explicitly requested that local artifact.
7. For mixed sources, convert only the local files and leave Drive objects on the MCP route.

## The trap this skill exists to prevent

**OCR-by-eye copy-paste** — manually retyping tables and headings from PDFs, losing structure and introducing typos. Always convert via MarkItDown, never re-key content from the source by hand.

## Process

### 1. Detect file format
Verify that the input is an existing local path, then check extension `.pdf`, `.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`, `.html`, `.jpg`, `.png`. Script `convert.sh` auto-detects from extension — no need to specify format. If the input is a Drive URL or ID, do not run the converter.

### 2. Run converter

**Method 1 — run script directly:**
```bash
# Convert PDF to MD (auto output = input_DD-MM-YYYY.md)
bash <skill-root>/scripts/convert.sh /path/to/file.pdf

# Convert with specific output base; script still appends date
bash <skill-root>/scripts/convert.sh /path/to/file.docx /tmp/output.md

# Convert Excel
bash <skill-root>/scripts/convert.sh /path/to/data.xlsx /tmp/data.md
```

Resolve `<skill-root>` from the directory containing the loaded `SKILL.md`. Do not assume the skill is located in `.claude`, `.codex`, `.gemini` or a specific home directory.

All new Markdown files use the `_DD-MM-YYYY` suffix based on `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` time, e.g., `FRS_20-07-2026.md`. Do not append the date twice if the basename already has the correct suffix. Do not rename existing files. If the user explicitly requests keeping the exact filename, run with `QA_PRESERVE_EXACT_FILENAME=1`.

**Method 2 — AI auto-detects and converts** (when user uploads a file in chat):
1. Detect file type (PDF, DOCX, ...)
2. Run `bash <skill-root>/scripts/convert.sh <file>`
3. Read the MD output file instead of the original file
4. Analyze the content and respond

**AI workflow example**:
```python
import os, subprocess
skill_root = os.environ['DOC_TO_MD_SKILL_DIR']
result = subprocess.run(
    ['bash', os.path.join(skill_root, 'scripts', 'convert.sh'),
     '/path/to/spec.pdf', '/tmp/spec.md'],
    capture_output=True, text=True
)
with open('/tmp/spec.md', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()
# Phân tích content thay vì parse PDF trực tiếp
```

### 3. Supported formats

| Format | Extension | Output quality |
|---|---|---|
| PDF | `.pdf` | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ - text + tables + structure |
| Word | `.docx`, `.doc` | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ - perfect |
| PowerPoint | `.pptx`, `.ppt` | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ - slides + notes |
| Excel | `.xlsx`, `.xls` | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ - tables + sheets |
| HTML | `.html`, `.htm` | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ |
| Images | `.jpg`, `.png`, `.gif` | ⭐⭐⭐ - OCR (requires Tesseract) |
| Audio | `.mp3`, `.wav` | ⭐⭐⭐ - transcription (requires Whisper) |
| CSV | `.csv` | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ |
| JSON/XML | `.json`, `.xml` | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ |
| ZIP | `.zip` | ⭐⭐⭐ - extract and convert each file |

### 4. Installation

First time running, the script auto-installs MarkItDown. If it fails, install manually:
```bash
pip3 install "markitdown[all]"
```

Optional dependencies per format:
- PDF: requires `pdfminer.six` (auto-installed with `[all]`)
- Image OCR: requires `tesseract` (`brew install tesseract` on Mac)
- Audio: requires `ffmpeg` + `whisper`

### 5. Example

**Document conversion:**
```bash
$ QA_ARTIFACT_DATE=20-07-2026 bash <skill-root>/scripts/convert.sh /project/spec/FRS.docx
🔄 Converting: /project/spec/FRS.docx → /project/spec/FRS_20-07-2026.md
📦 Installing MarkItDown...
🔄 Converting...
✅ Done: FRS_20-07-2026.md (45,231 bytes, 1,247 lines)
```

**AI usage after conversion:**
```python
with open('BCP_AI_SRS.md') as f:
    spec = f.read()
# Extract requirements
# "FR-M1-01: User registers account..."
# → generate test cases from requirement
```

## Red flags

| Symptom | Why it's wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Output MD missing table headers | MarkItDown can fail on scanned PDFs | Install Tesseract OCR or use a PDF with a text layer |
| Audio transcription returns empty text | Whisper not installed or ffmpeg bad path | Verify `ffmpeg` in PATH, install `openai-whisper` |
| Build wheel fails for `cryptography` on macOS | Missing OpenSSL dev headers + Rust | Use `--only-binary=:all:` (see Common mistakes) |
| Large PDF > 100 pages converts very slowly | MarkItDown processes each page sequentially | Split file or use a page range filter |

## Common mistakes

- **macOS — cryptography build error:** `pip3 install "markitdown[all]"` often fails with `Failed building wheel for cryptography`. Cause: OpenSSL dev headers + Rust are missing, and installing via brew hits `/usr/local` permissions (often blocked on corporate laptops). **Fix by using prebuilt wheel:**
  ```bash
  pip3 install --only-binary=:all: "markitdown[all]"
  ```
  Verify: `PYTHON_BIN=/usr/local/bin/python3.11 python3 -c "import cryptography; print('OK', cryptography.__version__)"`

- **If it still fails** (custom pyenv Python, very old macOS):
  - `brew install pkgconf openssl` (requires `/usr/local` ownership change — not recommended on corporate laptops)
  - Or Conda: `conda install -c conda-forge markitdown`

- **Manual retyping instead of converting** — loses table structure, introduces typos, wastes time. Always run `convert.sh` first.

- **Downloading Drive objects to convert when user only asked to read/analyze** — wrong source route and creates unnecessary local snapshots. Use `google-drive` MCP for in-place reading; only convert when user explicitly requests a local copy.

- **Uploading files to other cloud services** — MarkItDown processes locally, preserving privacy. Do not upload unless the user explicitly requests it.

- **Converting audio without Whisper installed** — script will fail silently or return empty. Install ffmpeg + openai-whisper first.

- **Large PDFs > 100 pages** — may take several seconds. Consider splitting or converting only relevant sections.

## References

- [scripts/convert.sh](scripts/convert.sh) — wrapper script với auto-install + PYTHON_BIN override
- [MarkItDown (Microsoft)](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown) — upstream open-source tool

# ego-browser

ego-browser là một **browser driver riêng** cho AI agents — không phải chỉ là fallback của Playwright. Nó cung cấp isolated task space kế thừa login state thật của user, phù hợp cho UI interaction và DOM observation. Network observation chi tiết (body, headers, timing) vẫn cần Chrome DevTools MCP hoặc Playwright MCP.

Trước khi dùng, chạy detect để xác nhận trạng thái:
```bash
node ego-browser/scripts/detect.mjs
```

Để hiểu đầy đủ CLI và helpers, đọc upstream skill tại thời điểm cài đặt:
```bash
cat "$(npx --yes skills which citrolabs/ego-lite 2>/dev/null)/ego-browser/SKILL.md" 2>/dev/null \
  || echo "upstream not installed — read https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/tree/main/skills/ego-browser"
```

## Khi nào dùng ego-browser

- Cần kế thừa login state thật của user (cookie, session, extension) mà không setup lại auth
- Playwright MCP không available trên môi trường hiện tại
- Test Jira, CRM, Admin portal, hay bất kỳ site đã login
- Khám phá UI nhanh, exploratory testing, thu thập snapshot
- macOS; ego lite đã install và pass `detect.mjs`

## Khi nào KHÔNG dùng ego-browser

- Cần request/response body đầy đủ, headers, timing, WebSocket → dùng Chrome DevTools MCP hoặc Playwright MCP
- Đang chạy Windows hoặc Linux → ego-browser unsupported; dùng Playwright MCP
- Cần viết automation script tái sử dụng → dùng `playwright-pom-automation`
- Cần native mobile traffic → dùng `mobile-qa`
- Playwright MCP available và không có lý do cụ thể để đổi → tiếp tục dùng Playwright MCP

## Capability matrix

| Capability | ego-browser | Ghi chú |
|---|---|---|
| UI interaction | ✅ primary | click, fill, type, scroll, drag |
| DOM snapshot | ✅ `snapshotText()` | text-based, full page |
| Screenshot | ✅ `captureScreenshot()` | png/jpeg |
| Network events cơ bản | ✅ `drainEvents()` | navigation, basic requests |
| Request/response body | ❌ | cần Chrome DevTools MCP hoặc Playwright MCP |
| WebSocket / SSE / timing | ❌ | cần Chrome DevTools MCP |
| Real login state | ✅ native | kế thừa từ user's ego lite browser |
| Platform | macOS only | arm64 và x64 |

Đọc chi tiết: [`references/CAPABILITIES.md`](references/CAPABILITIES.md)

## Hard gate — bắt buộc khi dùng login state thật

ego-browser kế thừa cookie, token và session thật của user. Phải tuân thủ:

1. **Không submit payment, order, hoặc transfer thật** trừ khi user yêu cầu rõ và xác nhận
2. **Không gửi email hoặc message thật** đến người thật
3. **Không delete hoặc wipe dữ liệu production**
4. **Không expose cookie, token, localStorage** trong output, log hoặc artifact
5. **Không chạy destructive test trên production URL** — xác nhận môi trường trước
6. **Luôn log environment, URL và space ID** trước mỗi action có tác dụng ngoài app
7. **Xác nhận user** trước action phá huỷ ngay cả khi trên staging
8. **Không claim network evidence từ Chrome DevTools** khi chạy cùng session khác

## Quick start

Dùng heredoc `ego-browser nodejs << 'EOF' ... EOF`. Không viết code ra file `.js` riêng.

```bash
# Kiểm tra ego-browser sẵn sàng
node ego-browser/scripts/smoke-test.mjs --url https://example.com

# Hoặc chạy trực tiếp
ego-browser nodejs <<'EOF'
const task = await useOrCreateTaskSpace('my-task')
cliLog('space: ' + task.id)
await openOrReuseTab('https://example.com', { wait: true, timeout: 20 })
cliLog(await snapshotText())
EOF
```

Helpers đầy đủ: xem upstream SKILL.md (link ở trên) hoặc [`references/CAPABILITIES.md`](references/CAPABILITIES.md).

## Tích hợp với qa-run

Khi `qa-run` dùng ego-browser làm driver:

```bash
node scripts/helpers/run-manifest.mjs start \
  --mode EXPLORATORY_ADHOC \
  --business-context qa-knowledge/context/business-execution-brief.json \
  --browser-driver ego-browser \
  --browser-observer ego-browser \
  --network-observer chrome-devtools-mcp
```

Kết hợp tối ưu khi cần login state thật + network evidence đầy đủ:
- **UI + DOM**: ego-browser
- **Network**: Chrome DevTools MCP attach vào cùng Chromium process

# GitHub MCP QA

Use the official remote endpoint `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/` for all GitHub toolsets or a scoped `/x/<toolset>` endpoint when fewer tools are sufficient. Keep authentication local to each user; never place OAuth credentials or PAT values in this repository.

## Route the operation

| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Local commit, branch, fetch, pull, push | Git CLI with SSH or HTTPS credentials |
| Repository, PR, Issue, Actions, run logs, security data through API | GitHub MCP with OAuth or PAT |
| Edit a workflow | Edit `.github/workflows/*.yml` locally, validate, commit and push |
| Observe or rerun a workflow | GitHub MCP `actions` tools after authentication |

Do not claim that an SSH key authenticates GitHub MCP. SSH and MCP/API authentication are separate.

## Install and diagnose

Select the guide for the active host:

- Codex: read [references/codex-github-mcp-vi.md](references/codex-github-mcp-vi.md)
- Antigravity: read [references/antigravity-github-mcp-vi.md](references/antigravity-github-mcp-vi.md)

For macOS, Linux, or WSL, configure the server with:

```bash
./github-mcp-qa/scripts/install-codex.sh --login
```

Use `--dry-run` before mutation. Codex defaults to PAT from `GITHUB_PAT_TOKEN`; use `--login` only when that Codex version can complete GitHub OAuth. Run the host-specific doctor after setup.

## Execute GitHub work

1. Resolve `owner/repo`, target branch, current account, and requested operation
2. Read repository state before any write
3. For local changes, inspect `git status`, preserve unrelated changes, and use Git CLI
4. For GitHub API changes, verify the authenticated account and repository permission first
5. Require explicit confirmation immediately before deleting repositories, branches, releases, packages, workflow artifacts, secrets, or changing security/organization settings
6. Read back the changed object or workflow run after mutation
7. Report the exact repository, branch, commit/run ID, status, and remaining blocker

## CI/CD rules

- Inspect existing workflows and repository conventions before creating a pipeline
- Pin action versions according to repository policy; never expose secrets in YAML, logs, artifacts, or prompts
- Give `GITHUB_TOKEN` only the workflow permissions required by its jobs
- Validate syntax and relevant tests locally before push
- Treat dispatch, rerun, cancel, deployment approval, secret rotation, and permission changes as state-changing operations
- Separate pipeline creation from production deployment authorization

## Authentication boundaries

- Prefer OAuth only when the active host supports the GitHub OAuth flow; otherwise use a fine-grained PAT from an environment variable or secret manager
- Use a fine-grained PAT only when OAuth is unavailable; store it in an environment variable or secret manager
- Treat `x/all` as all MCP toolsets, not unlimited GitHub account permission
- Respect organization SSO, GitHub App, PAT, branch-protection, ruleset, and Actions policies
- Clear the active host OAuth session or change the PAT environment when switching MCP identity
- Keep personal and company Git identities isolated with separate SSH keys and host aliases

Read [references/qa-mcp-stack-vi.md](references/qa-mcp-stack-vi.md) when selecting GitHub MCP alongside Chrome DevTools, k6, Postman, database read-only, and Slack.

When the user asks which QA MCP servers are connected or reports that a skill exists but its tool is missing, run `scripts/doctor-stack.sh --agent=<host>` before suggesting installation. Do not treat a configured server as loaded until a new host session exposes its tools and a read-only smoke test succeeds.

# Google Drive QA

Use this skill as the stable workflow layer. A skill does not itself grant Drive access: live private Drive CRUD uses the configured `google-drive` MCP, while local uploads can use the bundled user-OAuth script as a fallback.

If `ACCOUNT-PROFILE.md` exists beside this file, read it before selecting the Google account, OAuth credential path, MCP route, or fallback CLI. Create it from `ACCOUNT-PROFILE.example.md`; it is local routing metadata and must never contain credential values or be committed.

## Cross-model hard gates

Use these gates literally on every model:

1. Treat a bare Drive, Docs, Sheets, or Slides URL/ID as an implicit request to resolve and read that exact object; do not ask which skill to use or stop after explaining the skill
2. Parse an exact Drive URL or ID before searching by name
3. Read `references/ROUTING.md` and `references/CRUD.md`
4. Use the `google-drive` MCP for private Drive and native Docs, Sheets, or Slides CRUD
5. Resolve one exact object before a write; stop for ambiguity instead of selecting the first search result
6. Perform only the requested CRUD operation; a bare URL authorizes read-only inspection, not mutation
7. Read the affected object back and verify its ID, name, parent/location, and changed content or permission

Never substitute web search or a local same-named file for private Drive content. Never test deletion on real data.

## Route the request

1. Classify before acting:
   - Drive/Docs/Sheets/Slides URL or ID only → resolve and read metadata plus accessible content
   - URL/ID plus read/summarize/analyze language → perform that read-only operation
   - URL/ID plus explicit create/update/rename/move/copy/upload/share/delete language → perform only that mutation after exact-target checks
   - Google Sheet URL plus execute/run testcase language → use `qa-run` `SHEET_TESTCASE_EXECUTION`, with this skill handling Sheet CRUD
2. Read [references/ROUTING.md](references/ROUTING.md).
3. Read [references/CRUD.md](references/CRUD.md) for every Drive create, read, update, delete, permission, or native Google file request.
4. For private Drive access, use the configured `google-drive` MCP or the pre-built Python CLI scripts in `scripts/drive_crud.py`.
5. For Python CLI operations without MCP, run `python3 scripts/drive_crud.py <C|R|U|D> [options]`.
   - Read (`R`): `python3 scripts/drive_read.py <FILE_ID_OR_URL>` (exports & reads Docs, Sheets, Word, Excel, PDF directly from Cloud).
   - Create (`C`): `python3 scripts/drive_create.py --file <path> --folder-id <id> [--convert]` (uploads or creates items; `--convert` converts Word/Excel to Doc/Sheet).
   - Update (`U`): `python3 scripts/drive_update.py <FILE_ID_OR_URL> [--name <name>] [--move-to <folder_id>]`.
   - Delete (`D`): `python3 scripts/drive_delete.py <FILE_ID_OR_URL> [--permanent] [--yes]`.
6. For first-time Google Cloud and OAuth setup, read [references/GOOGLE_CLOUD_OAUTH_SETUP.md](references/GOOGLE_CLOUD_OAUTH_SETUP.md).
7. For an authentication error, read [references/AUTH.md](references/AUTH.md) and report the exact failing layer: MCP unavailable, OAuth credential missing, access token expired, refresh revoked, scope insufficient, or object permission denied.
8. Read [references/REPORTS.md](references/REPORTS.md) before summarizing or uploading QA reports.

## MCP rules

- Prefer the configured `google-drive` MCP for Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, and permission CRUD.
- If its tools are unavailable, say that the MCP is not loaded in the current session. Do not claim the object is missing and do not substitute public web search.
- If the MCP reports authorization required or expired, run the authentication checks in [references/AUTH.md](references/AUTH.md), then retry the same operation.
- Do not repeatedly search the repository for a Drive script when the request belongs to the MCP.

## Local OAuth rules

- `drive.file` is an upload-oriented scope. It does not provide general read access to every existing Drive file.
- Tokens with a refresh token normally refresh automatically. If Google returns `invalid_grant`, the consent was revoked or the refresh token is unusable; run the uploader with `--reauth` only when the user wants to start a new consent flow.
- Never print, copy, commit, or place OAuth client JSON or token JSON in a report.

## Output rules

- Identify the source file by name and link or ID.
- Preserve exact ticket IDs, testcase IDs, verdicts, counts, and evidence links.
- Distinguish source facts from inferences.
- For human-readable content created or updated through Drive CRUD, do not end sentences, list items, or testcase cells with `.` and do not insert emoji or icons.
- Preserve identifiers, URLs, filenames, folder names, sheet/tab names, formulas, code, numeric values, JSON keys, and API fields exactly; the prose-format rule must not mutate machine-readable data.
- Never overwrite a Drive file merely because a same-named file exists. Confirm replace/update semantics first.
- Treat create, upload, update, move, rename, copy, permission, and delete operations as external writes. Resolve the exact target first and follow the confirmation rules in [references/CRUD.md](references/CRUD.md).

# Mobile QA

Treat platform, OS, device class, lifecycle, and network state as explicit test dimensions. Never present emulator-only evidence as real-device coverage.

## Hard gates

1. Resolve the build artifact, application ID or bundle ID, environment, supported platforms and OS range, device scope, accounts, test data, and distribution authorization
2. Before a run that changes device or app state, record `Target`, `Operation`, `Required inputs`, `Write action`, and `Verification`
3. Verify the artifact checksum and installed build version before execution
4. Select the device matrix and lifecycle scope from [references/DEVICE_MATRIX.md](references/DEVICE_MATRIX.md)
5. Keep signing files, provisioning profiles, credentials, tokens, personal data, and raw device identifiers out of reports
6. Define cleanup for accounts, notifications, files, permissions, app data, sessions, and device state
7. Ask immediately before purchases, messages, calls, external notifications, account deletion, destructive data reset, or another material side effect
8. Do not claim coverage outside the executed device matrix
9. Intercept traffic only for an authorized app, environment, account, device, and domain scope
10. Treat CA installation, proxy changes, VPN profiles, Rewrite, Breakpoint, Map Local/Remote, throttling, replay, and request/response mutation as state changes with explicit cleanup
11. Redact authorization headers, cookies, tokens, credentials, personal data, and sensitive bodies before saving or sharing network evidence
12. Do not bypass certificate pinning in a release or third-party app; request an authorized debug build or report `BLOCKED: certificate_pinning`

## Route the request

- Use Appium MCP for interactive discovery, smoke, regression, exploratory checks, locator learning, gestures, evidence, and requested test-code generation
- Use `adb`, logcat, Android Studio, and UiAutomator2 for Android setup and diagnosis
- Use Xcode, `simctl`, device logs, WebDriverAgent, and XCUITest for iOS setup and diagnosis
- Use `scripts/scrcpy-wifi.sh` on macOS/Linux or `scripts/scrcpy-wifi.ps1` on Windows only to mirror an Android device; mirroring is not test automation or evidence by itself
- Use `scripts/scaffold-wdio.sh` when Appium MCP is unavailable but a deterministic WebdriverIO/Appium project is required
- Use `scripts/scaffold-mobile-ci.sh` to install the Android PR-emulator workflow and execution-target hard gate into a target GitHub repository
- Use `scripts/configure-appium-mcp.py --agent antigravity` to configure Appium MCP for Antigravity with an atomic JSON update and backup
- Use a licensed device-cloud integration only when the requested matrix requires devices unavailable locally
- Use native accessibility inspection and a real screen reader for accessibility verdicts
- Use Proxyman MCP for interactive macOS traffic inspection when its official MCP server is available; otherwise use its bundled CLI for session control and HAR export
- Use `mitmdump` as the primary open-source headless or CI network-capture engine
- Use Fiddler Everywhere MCP when its licensed MCP server is configured
- Use Charles headless/CLI or HTTP Toolkit UI/ADB interception only as explicit fallbacks

Read [references/APPIUM_MCP.md](references/APPIUM_MCP.md) before an Appium MCP run. Read [references/MOBILE_CI.md](references/MOBILE_CI.md) before adding or diagnosing mobile CI/CD. Read [references/MOBILE_NETWORK_INSPECTION.md](references/MOBILE_NETWORK_INSPECTION.md) before intercepting or modifying traffic, and use [references/PROXY_TOOL_MATRIX.md](references/PROXY_TOOL_MATRIX.md) to select an engine. Read [references/SCRCPY_WIFI.md](references/SCRCPY_WIFI.md) for Android Wi-Fi mirroring. On Windows, also read [references/WINDOWS_MOBILE_QA.md](references/WINDOWS_MOBILE_QA.md) before setup or execution. Read [references/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](references/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) only when setup or execution fails.

## Workflow

### 1. Establish readiness

Run the platform doctor:

- macOS/Linux: `scripts/mobile-doctor.sh --android`, `--ios`, or `--all`
- Windows: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/mobile-doctor.ps1 -Mode android`

Treat its MCP result as advisory because only the active MCP client can prove tool availability. Local iOS execution requires macOS and Xcode; route iOS requested from Windows to a macOS self-hosted runner or a licensed remote device farm.

For a local Appium MCP run:

1. Confirm the Appium MCP tools are loaded
2. Call `select_device` before creating a local session
3. Prepare an iOS simulator with `prepare_ios_simulator`, or prepare a real iOS device with `appium_prepare_ios_real_device`, when required
4. Create the session with `appium_session_management` and explicit capabilities
5. Record the returned `sessionId`, ownership, platform, OS, device class, and app build

If the tool surface is missing, classify the failing layer as `mcp_not_configured`, `auth_required`, `runtime_missing`, `mcp_not_loaded`, or `permission_denied`. Do not describe every failure as an Appium bug.

### 2. Prove install and launch health

Verify clean install, upgrade when in scope, first launch, permissions, authentication, foreground and background behavior, process restart, device restart when applicable, and uninstall cleanup.

Capture an initial screenshot and the device/app metadata before manipulating the flow.

### 3. Execute and verify each journey

For every action:

1. Locate by `accessibility id`
2. Fall back to `id`
3. Fall back to `-ios predicate string`, `-ios class chain`, or `-android uiautomator`
4. Inspect page source or generated locators if needed
5. Use `appium_gesture` with `action=scroll_to_element` before declaring an off-screen element missing

### 4. Inspect mobile network behavior

Correlate each network flow with the triggering UI step and verify:

- Method, host, path, status, content type, latency, size, caching, retry, and cancellation behavior
- Authentication and refresh flow without exposing secrets
- GraphQL operation name, error envelope, and partial-data behavior
- WebSocket handshake, reconnect, ordering, duplication, and disconnect recovery
- Offline, timeout, throttled, malformed, and server-error behavior only when those mutations are authorized

Export a sanitized HAR when the selected engine supports it, then run:

```text
python scripts/analyze-mobile-har.py /absolute/path/to/capture.har --format markdown
```

If HTTPS cannot be decrypted, distinguish missing CA trust, certificate pinning, mTLS, proxy bypass, VPN conflict, and unsupported protocol behavior. Do not silently weaken the app.

### 5. Capture evidence

- Capture screenshots at checkpoints and at every failure
- Use screen recording for timing-sensitive, gesture-heavy, crash, or interruption scenarios
- Capture logcat, iOS device logs, or crash reports for crash and ANR findings
- Keep `appium_screenshot.returnRawBase64` false so evidence is saved to a file
- Record the build, device class, OS, real or virtual status, capability set, locator strategy, and reproducibility with each finding
- Store only sanitized network summaries or HAR files; record proxy engine/version, capture scope, CA state, applied rules, and cleanup status

For CI or device farms, use an explicit trusted `remoteServerUrl` and explicit capabilities instead of local device discovery. Pass `sessionId` on every tool call when multiple sessions exist.

- Commit the Page Objects, selectors, specs, configuration, lockfile, and build adapter

# Pentest Run

Run evidence-led security assessments with explicit scope and human control

## Hard gates

1. Resolve the exact authorized target, owner, environment, time window, allowed techniques, exclusions and rate limit
2. Write the five-field execution contract before any network request: `Target`, `Operation`, `Required inputs`, `Write action`, `Verification`
3. Create or read `.pentest/engagement.md` using [references/ENGAGEMENT_CONTRACT.md](references/ENGAGEMENT_CONTRACT.md)
4. Run `bash scripts/doctor.sh` and record each available or unavailable tool
5. Start with passive or low-impact discovery and preserve the original request and response evidence
6. Ask for explicit approval immediately before every state-changing, concurrency, exploit-validation or high-volume action
7. Confirm a finding only after deterministic reproduction and a control comparison
8. Produce the finding and engagement summary using [references/FINDING_FORMAT.md](references/FINDING_FORMAT.md)

Do not install a missing tool, enable `/yolo`, widen scope, change accounts, persist access, exfiltrate data, evade monitoring or run destructive payloads without separate explicit authorization

## Routing

Read [references/TOOL_ROUTING.md](references/TOOL_ROUTING.md) before selecting a tool

- Use PentesterFlow as the primary CLI coordinator when it is installed and healthy
- Use recon-skills as methodology references selected for the current technology and vulnerability class
- Use Raccoon only for scoped host, DNS, service and content discovery with an explicit rate limit
- Use DockerScan for local or explicitly authorized Docker images, Dockerfiles, daemon configuration and runtime inspection
- Use GhidraGPT only for binaries the user supplied or explicitly authorized for reverse engineering
- Use Burp integration for user-captured traffic, replay and evidence; treat raw traffic and tokens as sensitive
- Use ordinary browser or HTTP tools only when the engagement contract allows them and the selected route needs them

Treat `source_available` and `available` as different states. A cloned repository may be read for methodology or inspected locally, but do not execute it as a scanner until its executable, dependencies and version checks are healthy

When the doctor reports an executable `available`, use the exact absolute `path=` from its output so local managed tools do not depend on the caller's shell PATH

If a named route is unavailable, report the exact missing executable, plugin, file or configuration and stop that route. Do not silently replace it with an unrelated scanner

## Risk levels

### Level 0: local and passive

Proceed after the engagement contract is complete

- Read supplied files, documentation, source and captures
- Inspect DNS and public metadata at low rate
- Analyze a local Docker image or supplied binary without executing it
- Draft hypotheses, coverage and reports

### Level 1: low-impact active discovery

Proceed only inside the authorized target and rate limit

- Request known public endpoints
- Fingerprint technologies and services
- Enumerate documented application behavior with test accounts
- Run non-destructive container configuration checks

### Level 2: exploit validation

Pause for explicit approval immediately before execution

- Cross-account authorization checks
- SSRF, SSTI, JWT, GraphQL or deserialization probes
- Race-condition and replay tests
- Requests that create, edit or delete application state
- Runtime Docker inspection or controlled exploitation

Use the smallest proof that establishes impact, prefer the user's own test account or object and compare pre-state with post-state

### Level 3: separately authorized only

Do not proceed without a written isolated-lab or engagement authorization that names the action

- Denial of service or resource exhaustion
- Password spraying, credential stuffing or brute force
- Persistence, lateral movement or privilege expansion beyond the proof target
- Data extraction beyond the minimum redacted sample
- Malware, destructive payloads or changes that are difficult to recover
- Evasion, anonymous routing or proxy rotation intended to bypass controls

## Execution workflow

### 1. Scope

Read or create the engagement contract. Resolve hostnames to the supplied scope before scanning. Keep production, staging, VPN, cloud accounts, containers and binaries as separate targets

### 2. Baseline

Capture target availability, identity, current role, observable state and rate-limit behavior before testing. Save commands and timestamps under `.pentest/evidence/`

### 3. Recon and enumeration

Run only the minimum route needed to map the requested surface. Maintain `.pentest/coverage.md` with assets, endpoints, roles, parameters, vulnerability classes and status values `covered`, `partial`, `blocked` or `not_covered`

### 4. Hypothesis and control

For each candidate issue, write the expected secure behavior, suspected weakness, one test request and one control request. Mark it `Candidate` until both are executed and compared

### 5. Validation

Request approval for Level 2 or Level 3 actions. Reproduce with deterministic commands, redact secrets and collect the smallest evidence needed. A scanner alert alone is never a confirmed finding

### 6. Reporting and learning

Write confirmed findings under `.pentest/findings/` and unresolved observations under `.pentest/candidates/`. Store reusable non-secret project lessons in `.pentest/knowledge.md`; never store passwords, tokens, cookies, private keys or raw personal data

## Completion checks

- Target and authorization match the engagement contract
- Every command stayed inside scope and rate limits
- Active actions have an approval record
- Every confirmed finding has reproduction evidence and a negative or control comparison
- Candidate findings are not reported as confirmed vulnerabilities
- Evidence is redacted and stored at deterministic paths
- Coverage gaps and blocked checks are explicit
- The final report separates observation, impact, confidence and remediation

## Resources

- [references/ENGAGEMENT_CONTRACT.md](references/ENGAGEMENT_CONTRACT.md) for scope and authorization fields
- [references/TOOL_ROUTING.md](references/TOOL_ROUTING.md) for deterministic tool selection
- [references/FINDING_FORMAT.md](references/FINDING_FORMAT.md) for evidence-backed reporting
- [scripts/doctor.sh](scripts/doctor.sh) for non-invasive tool and dependency checks

# Performance QA

Use one public skill and two internal engines. Never ask the user or intern to
select a separate JMeter skill.

For first-time human setup and usage, see [GUIDE.md](GUIDE.md).

## Deterministic flow

1. Run `python3 scripts/performance_orchestrator.py doctor`
2. Run `python3 scripts/performance_orchestrator.py discover --root <project-root>`
3. Resolve engine:
   - Exact `.jmx` → JMeter
   - Exact k6 `.js`, `.ts`, or `.mjs` → k6
   - `engine: auto` with exactly one discovered engine → that engine
   - Both engines or no script → ask only for the engine; do not guess
4. Copy [assets/run-config.example.yaml](assets/run-config.example.yaml) or run:
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/performance_orchestrator.py wizard --output run-config.yaml
   ```
5. Ask only fields required by the chosen workload model:
   - `concurrent-users`: users, ramp-up, hold, ramp-down, think time
   - `request-rate`: target rate, time unit, pre-allocated VUs, max VUs, duration
   - `total-iterations`: iterations, users, max duration, think time
6. Resolve p95, p99, maximum error rate, minimum throughput and abort behavior
7. Validate, display, and prepare without executing:
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/performance_orchestrator.py validate --config run-config.yaml
   python3 scripts/performance_orchestrator.py prepare \
     --config run-config.yaml \
     --project-root <project-root> \
     --output-root artifacts
   ```
8. Read back `run-config.yaml` and `run-plan.json`; show engine, target, workload,
   thresholds, approvals, smoke command, main command and artifact paths
9. Immediately before execution, obtain the approvals required below, then run:
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/performance_orchestrator.py run \
     --run-dir artifacts/<run-id> \
     --approve-load
   ```
10. The runner must execute one-user smoke first. Main load cannot start when
    smoke fails
11. Parse JTL or k6 JSON into `result.json`; generate `summary.md`,
    `summary.html`, engine-native report and redacted logs
12. Correlate latency/errors with CPU, memory, database, pool, queue, network,
    cache and downstream evidence before naming a bottleneck

## Hard gates

1. Resolve exact environment, owner, written authorization reference, target,
   workload, request mix/business flow, data, exclusions, cleanup, monitoring
   and abort conditions before load
2. A bare `.jmx`, JTL, k6 script or result file authorizes safe inspection only
3. Never run production without written authorization naming target and workload
   plus explicit approval immediately before execution
4. Any workload above one user, any request-rate load, and stress/spike/soak
   require `--approve-load` immediately before the main run
5. More than `safety.maxUsers` (default 100) also requires
   `--approve-high-load`; production also requires `--approve-production`
6. Never hardcode passwords, tokens, cookies, API keys or private keys in config,
   JMX, k6 script, commands, logs or reports; use environment placeholders
7. Always capture idle health and run one user/one iteration before load
8. Stop when smoke fails, service health fails, connectivity is lost, resource
   saturation appears, or an agreed abort condition is met
9. Assert status and business response under load; a fast incorrect response is
   a failure
10. Do not compare runs whose environment, dataset, cache state or workload model
    differs without disclosing the difference
11. JMeter GUI is for import/debug only; evidence-bearing runs use non-GUI mode
12. MCP/runtime availability never grants load authorization

## Engine resources

- Read [references/COMMON_CONFIG.md](references/COMMON_CONFIG.md) when defining or
  validating the common config
- Read [references/JMETER.md](references/JMETER.md) only for JMeter generation,
  correlation, Thread Group or JMX import details
- Read [references/K6.md](references/K6.md) only for k6 scenarios and environment
  mapping
- Read [references/RESULTS.md](references/RESULTS.md) when normalizing, comparing
  or interpreting reports
- Read [references/TOOL_ROUTING.md](references/TOOL_ROUTING.md) for browser
  timing, Chrome DevTools, Grafana and runner selection
- Read [references/MCP_SETUP.md](references/MCP_SETUP.md) only for Chrome
  DevTools MCP or k6 MCP setup/diagnosis

## Completion checks

- One common config and exact engine are recorded
- Authorization, workload and abort conditions are complete
- Generated JMX parses or generated k6 script passes static preparation
- One-user smoke passed before main load
- Raw and native engine outputs are retained when requested
- `result.json`, `summary.md` and `summary.html` agree on PASS/FAIL
- p95, p99, error rate and throughput have threshold verdicts
- Slow endpoints and top errors are reported when native data provides them
- Cleanup and recovery health are verified
- Bottleneck claims have correlated evidence and limitations

# Plane QA

Use the bundled CLI and scripts in this directory. Resolve every path relative to this `SKILL.md`; do not search the current project for another Plane implementation unless this skill's doctor reports that the bundled files are missing.

If `ACCOUNT-PROFILE.md` exists beside this file, read it before choosing a default account, workspace, project, or credential environment-variable name. Create it from `ACCOUNT-PROFILE.example.md`; it is local routing metadata and must never contain credential values or be committed.

## Cross-model hard gates

Use these gates literally on every model. Do not compress, reorder, or infer around them:

1. Treat a bare Plane URL or ticket ID as an implicit request to inspect/read that ticket; do not ask which skill to use or stop after explaining the skill
2. Resolve the exact target from the supplied URL; only use configured defaults when no URL was supplied
3. Run `scripts/doctor.sh` before every live read or write
4. Read the matching format reference before drafting content
5. Run the canonical script in dry-run mode when it supports `--dry-run`
6. Perform only the explicitly requested write; a bare URL authorizes read-only inspection, not mutation
7. Read back the ticket or comment and verify workspace, ticket reference, content, evidence count, and state

Use this state map without interpretation: `PASS → Done`, `FAILED → In Progress`, `BLOCKED → unchanged`, `new bug → Todo`. If a named state cannot be resolved, stop and report `BLOCKED`; never choose a similar-looking state.

## Route the request

1. Classify before acting:
   - Plane URL or ticket ID only → doctor and read the exact ticket
   - Plane URL or ticket ID plus retest, re-test, verify, kiểm tra lại, PASS, FAILED, or BLOCKED → doctor/read, then `qa-run` RETEST_PLUS, then return here for comment/state
   - Log/create/update/comment/state/report language → the matching explicit Plane operation
2. For any live Plane read or write, run `bash scripts/doctor.sh --url '<Plane URL>'` when the user supplied a URL. Otherwise run `bash scripts/doctor.sh`.
3. Read [references/MULTI_WORKSPACE.md](references/MULTI_WORKSPACE.md) when the user has multiple workspaces or supplies a Plane URL.
4. For reading a ticket or report, read [references/READING_PLANE.md](references/READING_PLANE.md) and preserve the source section order.
5. For creating or rewriting a bug, read [BUG_FORMAT.md](BUG_FORMAT.md) completely before drafting or posting.
6. For retest comments, PASS/FAILED/BLOCKED verdicts, or inline evidence, read [references/COMMENT_FORMAT.md](references/COMMENT_FORMAT.md) completely.
7. For daily or cycle reports, read [REPORT_FORMAT.md](REPORT_FORMAT.md) completely. Do not apply the bug template to a report.
8. Treat create, update, comment, assign, archive, and delete operations as external writes. Show the final payload or a dry run and obtain confirmation before executing unless the user explicitly asked to perform that exact write.

## Authentication

- Plane uses a personal API key, not a refreshable OAuth session. Never claim that the skill can refresh an expired or revoked Plane key.
- Never ask for or accept a Plane account password. API operations require only a Personal API Key.
- When a URL is supplied, parse its origin and workspace slug and select `PLANE_API_KEY_<NORMALIZED_WORKSPACE_SLUG>`, falling back to `PLANE_API_KEY`.
- Never print the selected key or store a new key in tracked files.
- On `401` or `403`, stop retrying, report that the key is missing, expired, revoked, or lacks access, and follow [references/AUTH.md](references/AUTH.md).
- Do not fall back to browser login credentials for API actions.

## Common commands

```bash
bash scripts/doctor.sh
bash scripts/doctor.sh --url 'https://plane.example.com/workspace-a/projects/<project-id>/issues/<issue-id>/'
./plane.sh issue list <project_id>
./plane.sh issue get <issue_uuid> <project_id>
python3 work-items/log-bug.py bug.json --dry-run
python3 work-items/log-bug.py bug.json
python3 comments/post-result.py result.json --dry-run
python3 comments/post-result.py result.json
python3 comments/post-inline.py --ref PROJ-102 --text "Retest PASS" --img evidence.png
```

Prefer `work-items/log-bug.py` over hand-built JSON because it validates and renders the team format consistently. Always run `--dry-run` before creating a bug.

Prefer `comments/post-result.py` for retest comments because it validates the verdict and renders evidence inline. Use `comments/post-inline.py` only for free-form comments.

## Output rules

- Return a readable QA summary, not raw Plane JSON, unless the user asks for JSON.
- Keep title, status, priority, assignees, ticket URL, description sections, comments, and evidence distinct.
- Do not invent missing Expected, Actual, testcase IDs, assignees, or evidence.
- Never include passwords, API keys, cookies, or OAuth tokens in a ticket or report.
- Use Vietnamese with diacritics for content. Do not add emoji or icons to Plane content.
- Do not end human-readable sentences or list items with `.`. Preserve identifiers, URLs, filenames, numeric values, and machine-readable fields exactly.
- Standardize retest verdicts as exactly `PASS`, `FAILED`, or `BLOCKED`; never mix `FAIL` and `FAILED`.
- Keep retest comments concise: PASS contains only Result + Conclusion + inline images; FAILED adds only Actual + Expected; BLOCKED adds only Blocker. Never include Environment, Steps, Observed, Check, an Evidence text label, evidence filenames, internal suite names, browser mode, job IDs, or coverage narration unless the user explicitly asks.
- Create every new bug in `Todo`.
- After a retest result of `PASS`, post the evidence comment and move the ticket to `Done`.
- After a retest result of `FAILED`, post the evidence comment and move the ticket to `In Progress`.
- Do not change state automatically for BLOCKED.
- Prefer a supplied Plane URL over the configured default workspace. Never post to the default workspace when a URL identifies another workspace.
