---
name: playwright-pom-automation
description: Scaffold or extend Playwright Page Object Model automation for UI, API, or performance tests and QA CI. Trigger on writing Playwright tests/specs, Page Object Model, selectors, automation scaffolding, Allure, or CI setup; do not require the skill name. Keep selectors out of specs. Not for ad-hoc exploratory clicks, ticket retest execution, or production app debugging; use qa-run for those.
---

# Playwright POM Automation

**Core principle:** All selectors must go through a Page Object — never write `page.locator()` directly in spec files.

Covers 4 test types: **UI · API · Performance · CI/CD**, plus **Data-Driven Testing (DDT)** and parallel-safe test-data isolation. **Project-agnostic**: do NOT hardcode domain/URL/business logic.

> **When to use**: When the user wants to automate web/API tests or set up a test pipeline.
> **Different from** `qa-run` (live AI-driven exploratory) and `testcase-template` (testcase documents): this skill = **deterministic test-as-code running in CI**.
> **API key**: shared from `../config/api_keys.json` (see scripts/ai_provider.py).

## The trap this skill exists to prevent

**Flat selector soup** — tests with no POM layer, raw `page.locator()` chains scattered across spec files, leading to brittle suites that break on every UI redesign. Centralize selectors in `selectors/` repo, route through Page Object classes, spec files import from there.

## Process

### 1. Quick start
Read the **Decision tree** below → pick the right reference → copy the template → adapt.

### 2. Decision tree

| What the user wants | Read reference | Copy template |
|---|---|---|
| UI test, page object, locator, click/fill flow | `references/ui-testing.md` | `pages/base.page.ts`, `pages/example.page.ts`, `tests/ui/example.ui.spec.ts` |
| API test, HTTP request, auth/token, schema | `references/api-testing.md` | `fixtures/api-client.ts`, `tests/api/example.api.spec.ts` |
| Functional/E2E, business flow spanning UI+API | `references/ui-testing.md` + `references/api-testing.md` | `tests/functional/example.functional.spec.ts` |
| Data-driven/parameterized test, dataset, parallel data isolation | `references/data-driven-testing.md` | `fixtures/data-driven.ts`, `test-data/cases/login.cases.ts`, `tests/ui/example.data-driven.ui.spec.ts` |
| Perf/load/timing/SLA | `references/performance-testing.md` | `tests/performance/k6-load-test.js` (Tier 2) |
| Selector repo, centralized locators | (below) → `selectors/login.selectors.ts`, `selectors/index.ts` | - |
| Pipeline, CI/CD, Jenkins, GitHub Actions, schedule | `references/cicd.md` | `github-actions-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `playwright.config.ts` |

### 3. Standard project structure (POM, separated folders)
```
project-root/
├── tests/
│   ├── ui/            # *.ui.spec.ts        — per-page/component browser tests
│   ├── api/           # *.api.spec.ts       — request-level API tests
│   ├── functional/    # *.functional.spec.ts— E2E business flows
│   └── performance/   # *.perf.spec.ts (Tier 1) + k6/*.js (Tier 2)
├── pages/             # Page Object classes (POM) — one class per page
├── selectors/         # Centralized selector repo (NEW) ← single source of truth
├── fixtures/          # Auth, isolated runtime data, API request context
├── test-data/         # Versioned typed datasets/cases (read-only inputs)
├── testdata/          # Runtime-generated data (gitignored)
├── utils/             # Config, generators, allure helpers
├── reports/           # html/, allure-results/, allure-report/
├── playwright.config.ts
└── package.json       # scripts: test:ui / test:api / test:functional / lint
```

**When to use which folder**:
- `tests/ui/` - one page/component, one intent, fast, browser-driven
- `tests/api/` - one endpoint, request-level, no browser
- `tests/functional/` - full business flow spanning multiple steps
- `tests/performance/` - Tier 1 Playwright + Tier 2 k6

### 4. Define selector strategy (centralized repo)
**ALL locators must live in `selectors/`** — single source of truth. When UI changes, update one place; page objects and specs pick up automatically.

```
selectors/
├── login.selectors.ts
├── dashboard.selectors.ts
├── ...
└── index.ts           # barrel export
```

Each `<feature>.selectors.ts` exports:
1. **Raw selector strings** - `id`, `xpath`, `css` (when user specifies explicitly)
2. **Locator factory** - `getByRole/getByLabel/getByTestId` (preferred)

**Strategy priority** (most stable → most brittle):
1. `getByRole` / `getByLabel` / `getByTestId` (⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐) - ALWAYS FIRST PRIORITY
2. `id` (`#email`) - ⭐⭐⭐⭐
3. `xpath` - ⭐⭐
4. `css class` (`.btn-primary`) - ⭐ - AVOID, usually auto-generated

**Pattern for Page Object** (self-healing when UI changes):
```typescript
// pages/base.page.ts
protected heal(primary, fallbacks, description) {
  return primary.or(...fallbacks.map(f => f.describe(`fallback for: ${description}`)));
}

protected get loginBtn() {
  return this.heal(
    this.page.getByRole('button', { name: /login|đăng nhập/i }),
    [
      this.page.getByTestId('login-submit'),
      this.page.locator('#login-btn'),
      this.page.getByText('Đăng nhập', { exact: true }),
    ],
    'login button'
  );
}
```

### 4b. TypeScript `readonly` pattern (mandatory cho mọi POM)

**Mục đích:** Ngăn selector hoặc locator bị gán đè ngoài ý muốn — tương đương `private final` + `static final` trong Java/TestNG.

| Vị trí | Pattern TypeScript | Tương đương Java |
|---|---|---|
| Raw selector string | `export const sel = { id: '#btn' } as const` | `public static final String BTN = "#btn"` |
| Locator object trong POM | `private readonly locs: LoginLocators` | `private final LoginLocators locs` |
| Expose locator ra spec | `get submitButton(): Locator { return this.locs.submitButton; }` | `public WebElement getSubmitButton() { return submitButton; }` |

**Rule bắt buộc:**
- Tất cả selector file dùng `as const` ở object cuối.
- Tất cả Page Object class dùng `private readonly locs` — **KHÔNG** dùng `public locs` hay `protected locs`.
- Expose ra ngoài chỉ qua `getter` — không expose raw field public.
- Spec KHÔNG được import `buildLoginLocators` trực tiếp — phải qua Page Object.

### 4c. Annotations kiểu TestNG (mapping sang Playwright + Allure)

| TestNG Java | Playwright TypeScript | Mục đích |
|---|---|---|
| `@Test(groups="smoke")` | `test('name @smoke', ...)` + `--grep @smoke` | Group/tag để filter CI |
| `@BeforeClass` | `test.beforeAll(async () => {})` | Setup 1 lần cho cả describe block |
| `@AfterClass` | `test.afterAll(async () => {})` | Teardown / cleanup data sau cả block |
| `@BeforeMethod` | `test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {})` | Reset state trước mỗi test |
| `@AfterMethod` | `test.afterEach(async ({ page }, info) => {})` | Screenshot on fail, cleanup per-test |
| `@Test(enabled=false)` | `test.skip(() => condition, 'reason')` | Bỏ qua test theo điều kiện |
| `@Severity(CRITICAL)` | `allure.severity('critical')` | Mức độ nghiêm trọng của test |
| `@Feature("Login")` | `allure.feature('Login')` | Nhóm theo chức năng |
| `@Story("Happy path")` | `allure.story('Happy path')` | Sub-feature / user story |
| `@Owner("QA Team")` | `allure.owner('QA Team')` | Người sở hữu test |
| `@Description("...")` | `allure.description('...')` | Mô tả chi tiết |
| `@Step("Click login")` | `await allure.step('Click login', async () => {})` | Bước test hiện trong report |

**Rule bắt buộc:**
- Mọi spec file phải có ít nhất `allure.severity` + `allure.feature` + `allure.story`.
- Mọi test quan trọng phải wrap action chính bằng `allure.step(...)`.
- `afterEach` phải có block chụp screenshot khi test fail (xem template).
- Không dùng `test.only()` trong code commit lên CI (bẫy chỉ chạy 1 test).

### 5. Build Page Object classes (POM conventions)
| Convention | Details |
|---|---|
| 1 class = 1 page | File `login.page.ts` → class `LoginPage` |
| Locators in `selectors/` | Page objects import from `../selectors`. DO NOT hardcode locator in page |
| Action methods NO `expect()` | Page object = click/fill/read + return. **Assertions in spec file**. |
| `BasePage` | Shared helpers: `waitForLoad`, navigation, `waitForResponse`, text extraction |
| `data-testid` | Name as `<component>-<element>`, consistent with FE team |

### 6. Add API layer (API testing conventions)
- Default to using Playwright `request` fixture (`APIRequestContext`).
- Validate response schema with `zod` (priority) — fail fast on contract drift
- Auth/token fixture reusable: worker-scoped token/storage state, with a standalone request context and optional per-slot account pool
- CRUD lifecycle: create → use → delete in the same test's `finally`/fixture teardown. Use `afterAll` only for a serial, worker-owned lifecycle

### 7. Add Data-Driven Testing + parallel isolation

Separate two kinds of data:

1. **Case data** — versioned, typed, read-only rows under `test-data/cases/`
2. **Runtime data** — unique entities created by `fixtures/data-driven.ts`

Generate one Playwright test per case at collection time with a synchronous `for...of`. Every case must have a unique stable ID in the test title. Never let two parallel tests mutate the same account, record, cart, tenant, filename, or JSON store.

The runtime namespace must include:

```text
<runId>-<project>-p<parallelIndex>-w<workerIndex>-t<testIdHash>-r<retry>-e<repeatEachIndex>
```

Rules:
- Use the test-scoped `testData` fixture for unique email/string/resource keys
- Use `TEST_ACCOUNTS_JSON` to allocate a different account per parallel slot when scenarios mutate account-owned state
- Do not cycle/reuse an undersized account pool; fail with a clear configuration error
- Store runtime JSON in a namespace-specific file; never use one shared read-modify-write JSON file across workers
- Cleanup per test in fixture teardown/`afterEach`; use `afterAll` only for resources owned exclusively by that worker
- A browser context is isolated, but backend data is not; fresh contexts alone do not prevent conflicts
- Retries must create a new retry-scoped identity and cleanup only resources created by that attempt

See `references/data-driven-testing.md` for the full pattern and templates.

### 8. Add performance harness (optional — 2 tiers)
| Tier | When | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (Playwright) | Smoke perf gate, 1 user, in main suite | Playwright native (`page.timing`, `performance`) |
| 2 (k6) | Need >1 user, p95/p99 SLA, run separately | k6 |

**Escalate Tier 1 → 2 when**: >1 concurrent user needed, formal p95/p99 threshold, standalone CI job.
See `references/performance-testing.md` for template + escalation matrix.

### 9. Wire up Allure + CI (reporting & platform-NEUTRAL CI/CD)

**Reporting — Allure:**
- Annotate with `allure.step()`, `allure.attachment()` in UI/API/perf tests
- Playwright reporter: `allure-playwright`
- k6 -> Allure via JSON output + converter (or Grafana for live dashboard)
- `reports/` structure: `html/`, `allure-results/`, `allure-report/`

**CI/CD — platform selection:**
| Platform | When |
|---|---|
| **Jenkins** | `Jenkinsfile` exists in the repo |
| **GitHub Actions** | `.github/workflows/` exists |
| **New / none** | Ask user to choose platform before generating |

**5 standard stages** (different syntax, same logic):
1. Checkout code
2. Install (`npm ci`) + cache `node_modules` & Playwright browsers
3. Lint (optional, fail-fast)
4. `test:ui` + `test:api` in parallel
5. Publish Allure report

**k6**: run standalone job/stage, DO NOT block main pipeline.

**Secrets** (token, BASE_URL, TEST_USER/PASS):
- GitHub Actions → Repository Secrets (`secrets.*`)
- Jenkins → Credentials (`credentials('id')`)
- **DO NOT hardcode** in pipeline file or commit

### 10. Setup (one-time per project)
```bash
npm init -y
npm i -D @playwright/test allure-playwright zod
npx playwright install chromium      # + firefox / webkit if needed
# Tier 2: brew install k6 (mac) / see `references/performance-testing.md` (Linux/Windows)

# Add scripts to package.json
# "test:ui":        "playwright test --grep @ui"
# "test:api":       "playwright test --grep @api"
# "test:functional":"playwright test --grep @functional"
# "allure:gen":     "allure generate reports/allure-results -o reports/allure-report --clean"
# "lint":           "tsc --noEmit && eslint ."
```

### 11. Tagging convention
```typescript
test('login happy path @ui', async ({ page }) => { ... });
test('create user @api', async ({ request }) => { ... });
test('order flow @functional', async ({ page }) => { ... });
```
Filter:
- `npx playwright test --grep @ui`
- `npx playwright test --grep @api`
- `npx playwright test --grep @functional`

### 12. Self-check before delivering
- [ ] **`selectors/` repo created** for every page — NO hardcoded locators
- [ ] Page Object has NO `expect()` in action methods
- [ ] CRUD tests clean exact created IDs in `finally`/fixture teardown; `afterAll` is limited to worker-owned serial lifecycles
- [ ] DDT rows are typed, read-only, have unique stable IDs, and generate one test per row
- [ ] Mutating parallel tests use `testData` namespace or a non-shared account from `TEST_ACCOUNTS_JSON`
- [ ] Runtime stores/files are isolated by worker/test; no shared JSON read-modify-write
- [ ] Retry/repeat data keys include `retry` and `repeatEachIndex`
- [ ] `data-testid` named by convention `<component>-<element>`
- [ ] CI/CD has 2 platform templates: Jenkins + GitHub Actions
- [ ] Secrets via env vars/credentials, NOT hardcoded
- [ ] Allure annotations (step, attachment) for UI/API/perf
- [ ] Tests **sorted by type order** (if multiple types)
- [ ] Cover metadata correct (especially **C3 = project code**)
- [ ] Dropdown I (Results) + J (Priority) working
- [ ] Procedure has numbered steps; Expected is specific and measurable

## Red flags

| Symptom | Why it's wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Spec uses `page.locator('.btn-primary')` directly in spec | CSS class auto-generated, brittle | Move to `selectors/`, use `getByRole`/`getByTestId` |
| Page Object method has `expect()` inside | Action methods must be purely return, assertions in spec | Extract expect to spec file |
| Test creates data but no cleanup | DB pollution, subsequent tests fail due to old data | Delete exact owned IDs in `finally`/fixture teardown |
| DDT loop reuses one mutable payload object | Rows/workers overwrite each other | Keep case rows `readonly`; build a fresh runtime payload inside each test |
| Parallel tests reuse one account/record/cart | Backend state conflicts although browser contexts are fresh | Allocate per-worker accounts or create per-test resources with `testData` |
| Workers write the same JSON file | Lost updates/corrupt JSON from read-modify-write races | Include the data namespace in the filename; never share mutable runtime files |
| Fixture says “per worker” but has no `{ scope: 'worker' }` | Fixture actually runs per test | Declare a worker fixture and avoid test-scoped dependencies |
| CI/CD hardcodes `API_BASE_URL` or credentials in YAML | Secret leak, cannot be rotated | Use `secrets.*` (GitHub) or `credentials()` (Jenkins) |
| Test only asserts `status === 200` | Does not verify business rule, only checks if route responds | Add schema validation (zod), check critical fields |
| Tier 1 perf test runs 50 concurrent users | Playwright cannot scale | Escalate to k6 (Tier 2) |

## Common mistakes

- **Project-agnostic**: sample code must NOT contain specific domain/URL/business logic. Each project adapts.

- **New scripts must be idempotent**: running multiple times must not create stale data. Use `withRevert()`, fixture teardown, or exact-ID cleanup in `finally`.

- **JSON config** where possible instead of hardcoding URL/credentials.

- **Tagging convention**: use `@ui`, `@api`, `@functional`, `@performance` to filter. No tag = no filter = CI runs everything every time.

- **Allure annotations**: skipping `allure.step()` = report hard to debug. Tag every meaningful step.

- **API key**: one shared config file `../config/api_keys.json` (gitignored), used by all 3 skills. See [README.md](../README.md).

- **Self-check is critical**: AI often forgets cleanup hooks, hardcodes secrets, or omits the selector repo. Run through the full checklist before committing.

# Postman

Read [QUICK_REF.md](QUICK_REF.md) for UI marketplace installation, free API key generation, and quick authentication steps.

Use the official remote Postman MCP server for resource management. Use the bundled Postman CLI and Newman runtimes for reproducible collection execution.

## First-use bootstrap

1. Resolve the active host as `antigravity` or `codex`
2. Before changing local configuration, state:
   - `Target`: the exact MCP config or Codex MCP entry
   - `Operation`: add or enable `mcpServers.postman`
   - `Required input`: Postman account login in the OAuth browser
   - `Write action`: merge only the Postman entry and back up an existing Antigravity config
   - `Verification`: config read-back followed by a read-only workspace listing
3. Run:

```bash
python3 scripts/bootstrap.py --agent=<antigravity|codex>
```

The script is idempotent. Run it again when Postman tools are missing. Use `--check` for a read-only configuration check and `--dry-run` to preview the target and payload

4. For Antigravity, fully restart the IDE, run `/mcp`, select `postman`, and complete OAuth
5. For Codex, run `codex mcp login postman` when the bootstrap reports that login is required
6. Continue only after this read-only smoke test succeeds:

```text
List the Postman workspaces available to the active account without changing anything
```

OAuth consent is the only required user interaction for the US endpoint. Never request, print, or store the user's Postman password. Never commit API keys, access tokens, refresh tokens, cookies, or OAuth browser data

## Collection runtime

Run the runtime doctor before collection execution:

```bash
python3 scripts/runner.py doctor
```

Use the unified runner instead of assembling CLI commands manually:

```bash
python3 scripts/runner.py run <collection-path-or-id> \
  --environment <environment-path-or-id> \
  --bail \
  --report-dir evidence/postman
```

Engine selection is deterministic:

1. Prefer Postman CLI for every supported collection
2. Fall back to Newman only for JSON collection v2 or v2.1
3. Block Newman for Postman v3 YAML collections
4. Preserve the selected engine's exit code for CI

The runner creates `console.log` when `--report-dir` is supplied. For compatible v2 collections it also creates `report.json` and `junit.xml`. Authenticate the Postman CLI only when a cloud collection ID, cloud result upload, monitor, or another authenticated command requires it:

```bash
python3 scripts/runner.py login
```

Local collection paths do not require a Postman API key. Do not place API keys in collection URLs or command arguments; use the Postman CLI login flow or a protected CI secret

## Endpoint selection

- Use `minimal` by default for workspaces, collections, environments, and specifications
- Use `code` only for client-code and API-context workflows
- Use `full` only when a required tool is absent from `minimal`
- Use `--region=eu` only for an EU Postman account; EU requires an API key supplied through a protected environment or secret manager

Change the mode deterministically:

```bash
python3 scripts/bootstrap.py --agent=<agent> --mode=<minimal|code|full> --replace-endpoint
```

## Operation workflow

1. Resolve the exact account, team, workspace, collection, environment, specification, mock, or monitor
2. Use read-only discovery before any mutation
3. Record a mutation contract with target, operation, required inputs, write action, and verification
4. Execute only the requested Postman operation
5. Read the object back and verify its ID, parent workspace, name, and changed content

Route contract validation against a live implementation to `api-contract-qa`. Route explicit testcase document creation to `testcase-template`. Execute collections through `scripts/runner.py`

## Failure classification

- `mcp_not_configured`: run `scripts/bootstrap.py`
- `mcp_not_loaded`: restart the host and open `/mcp`
- `auth_required`: complete OAuth with the intended Postman account
- `workspace_permission_denied`: verify account, team, and workspace membership
- `tool_not_enabled`: switch endpoint mode only when the requested operation requires it
- `runtime_missing`: run dependency setup, then `scripts/runner.py doctor`
- `incompatible engine=newman collection=v3`: use Postman CLI

Do not report the integration as working based only on valid JSON. Require a successful read-only Postman response

---
name: qa-run
description: Execute risk-driven browser QA using business logic recovered from source code, saved QA knowledge, requirements and runtime evidence, with same-session network/console observation. Trigger on app or repository discovery, exploratory/ad-hoc testing, sanity/regression, Plane ticket retest, Sheet testcase execution, UI/UX, browser response errors, business-flow or system-logic analysis, and release sign-off; do not require the skill name. Rank evidence-linked charters instead of generic clicking, compose RETEST_PLUS and SHEET_EXECUTION_PLUS, and write verified knowledge back after execution. Not for writing automation, native-mobile traffic interception, or testcase documents.
---

# QA Run

**Core principle:** Chạy đúng phạm vi đúng lúc — không full regression mỗi cycle.

Resolve `<skill-root>` from the directory containing the loaded `SKILL.md`. **Data is fetched based on the working directory** (cwd or `QA_DATA_DIR`): `.env`, `auth.json`, `evidence/` are in the tested project folder — DO NOT mutate the skill folder. When loading knowledge, prioritize `qa-knowledge/knowledge-index.json` before reading specific scope files.

> **When to use**: discovering new bugs, verifying bugs, ad-hoc UI/API poking on a web app, sanity/risk-based recurring runs, regression (fixed testcases) placed in the project instance.
> **API key**: shared from `../config/api_keys.json` (see scripts/ai_provider.py) — NO key needed if using Copilot Pro/Antigravity/Claude Code CLI.

## Workflow composition router

Choose one entrypoint, then expand every required layer in its stack. Layers are internal capabilities of the single public `qa-run` skill, not separate skills.

```text
DISCOVERY_CORE =
  Scoped Business Discovery + Exploratory + Ad-hoc + UI/UX

RETEST_PLUS =
  Original Retest + Sanity + Impacted Regression + DISCOVERY_CORE

SHEET_EXECUTION_PLUS =
  Sheet Testcase Execution + Sanity + Impacted Regression + DISCOVERY_CORE
  + Original Retest only for rows linked to a ticket or previous failure

BROWSER_OBSERVABILITY =
  Same-session Network + Console + Page Error correlation
  Applied to every live browser stack without changing DISCOVERY_CORE

TEST_INTELLIGENCE =
  Requirement + Runtime Knowledge + Current Source + UI Observation
  -> Provenance-aware Business Brief -> Ranked Risks -> Exploratory Charters
```

| User entrypoint | Required stack | Read now |
|---|---|---|
| Exploratory, ad-hoc, bug hunting, UI/UX or business discovery | `DISCOVERY_CORE` | [references/TEST-INTELLIGENCE.md](references/TEST-INTELLIGENCE.md) and [references/PROCESS-GUIDE.md](references/PROCESS-GUIDE.md) |
| Plane ticket plus retest, re-test, verify, PASS, FAILED or BLOCKED | `RETEST_PLUS` | [references/RETEST-PLUS.md](references/RETEST-PLUS.md) and [references/PROCESS-GUIDE.md](references/PROCESS-GUIDE.md) |
| Google Sheet URL/ID plus execute or run testcases | `SHEET_EXECUTION_PLUS` | [references/TESTCASE_SHEET_SCHEMA.json](references/TESTCASE_SHEET_SCHEMA.json), [references/SHEET_WORKER_RESULT_SCHEMA.json](references/SHEET_WORKER_RESULT_SCHEMA.json), [references/RETEST-PLUS.md](references/RETEST-PLUS.md), and [references/PROCESS-GUIDE.md](references/PROCESS-GUIDE.md) |
| Sanity, smoke, impacted or recurring regression | `SANITY_REGRESSION_PLUS = Sanity + Impacted Regression + DISCOVERY_CORE` | [references/TEST-INTELLIGENCE.md](references/TEST-INTELLIGENCE.md) and [references/PROCESS-GUIDE.md](references/PROCESS-GUIDE.md) |
| First exploration of an app or feature | `APP_BASELINE_DISCOVERY = DISCOVERY_CORE` at app/feature scope | [references/TEST-INTELLIGENCE.md](references/TEST-INTELLIGENCE.md) and [references/PROCESS-GUIDE.md](references/PROCESS-GUIDE.md) |
| Analyze repository business logic | `REPO_BUSINESS_DISCOVERY`; add `DISCOVERY_CORE` when a live runtime is in scope | [references/TEST-INTELLIGENCE.md](references/TEST-INTELLIGENCE.md), [references/PIPELINE.md](references/PIPELINE.md), and [references/GRAPHIFY-EFFECTIVE-HTML.md](references/GRAPHIFY-EFFECTIVE-HTML.md) |
| Reconcile UI with source, docs or runtime | `UI_BUSINESS_RECONCILIATION + DISCOVERY_CORE` | [references/PIPELINE.md](references/PIPELINE.md) and [references/PROCESS-GUIDE.md](references/PROCESS-GUIDE.md) |
| Write Playwright automation or POM | Exit `qa-run` | Route to `playwright-pom-automation` |

Create a ledger row for every expanded layer. Do not conclude the parent workflow while any required layer lacks `PASS`, `FAILED`, `BLOCKED`, `PARTIAL`, or `N/A` with a reason.

For every live browser route, also create one `BROWSER_OBSERVABILITY` ledger row and read [references/BROWSER-OBSERVABILITY.md](references/BROWSER-OBSERVABILITY.md). Use the observer attached to the same page/session as the UI driver. Route native Android/iOS traffic to `mobile-qa`.

Before every executable browser route, build `TEST_INTELLIGENCE`. When the source repository is locally available, pass it to the canonical preparation command so stale or missing source knowledge is refreshed before risk selection. Execute ranked charters; do not replace them with a generic element checklist.

Load optional references only when their condition occurs:

- Tool choice is unresolved → [references/MCP-CHEATSHEET.md](references/MCP-CHEATSHEET.md)
- Project accounts, environment or Plane handoff must be bootstrapped → [references/PROJECT-SETUP.md](references/PROJECT-SETUP.md)
- Test data is the current blocker → [references/TEST-DATA.md](references/TEST-DATA.md)
- A workflow step failed → [references/COMMON-MISTAKES.md](references/COMMON-MISTAKES.md)
- Playwright was proven unavailable → [references/ANTIGRAVITY-FALLBACK.md](references/ANTIGRAVITY-FALLBACK.md)
- A verdict is shallow, contradictory or unsupported → [references/INTELLIGENCE-BOOST.md](references/INTELLIGENCE-BOOST.md)
- Repository-wide graph, cross-file impact, call-flow diagram or interactive intelligence report is requested → [references/GRAPHIFY-EFFECTIVE-HTML.md](references/GRAPHIFY-EFFECTIVE-HTML.md)

Treat `qa-run` as one public skill. Never load or expose `vendor/**/SKILL.md`; vendor code is an optional development dependency, not a user-selectable QA skill.

## Cross-model hard gates

Apply the following exact order for all models, especially fast or small-context models:

1. Select the user entrypoint, expand its complete workflow stack, and initialize a ledger row for every required layer before opening the browser. If the route exits to another skill, stop `qa-run`.
2. **[BEFORE BROWSER — PREPARE test intelligence]** Derive the narrow feature slug from the ticket, Sheet row, URL, or user scope. If source is available, resolve its exact repository root. Run:
   ```bash
   node scripts/helpers/prepare-test-intelligence.mjs \
     --intent <RETEST_TICKET|SHEET_TESTCASE_EXECUTION|SANITY_REGRESSION|EXPLORATORY_ADHOC> \
     --scope <feature-slug> \
     --repo <source-repo-if-available> \
     --target <route-or-ticket-url-if-known> \
     --expected <ticket-or-testcase-expected-if-known> \
     --role <role-if-known> \
     --impact <comma-separated-impacted-areas-if-known>
   ```
   Read both generated files under `qa-knowledge/context/`. `Business Execution Brief` is the machine gate and risk model:
   - `READY` → use its exact execution contract, `knowledge_health`, fact-level `source_evidence`, ranked `risk_inventory` and `exploratory_charters`
   - `NEEDS_DISCOVERY` → run only scoped runtime/UI discovery needed by `missing_required`, write knowledge, then rebuild the brief
   - `BLOCKED` → stop normal execution and report `missing_required`; never invent a route, role, rule, flow or expected result
   - Source facts remain static/document-derived until runtime confirms them. Discovery modes may start without `READY` only to produce missing knowledge
   - Execute high-priority charters first. Branch only when evidence changes the risk model; record why a charter was added, deferred or stopped
3. **Initialize Run Manifest** only after the business gate:
   ```bash
   node scripts/helpers/run-manifest.mjs start \
     --mode <MODE> \
     --business-context qa-knowledge/context/business-execution-brief.json \
     --browser-driver <auto|playwright-mcp|ego-browser|chrome-devtools-mcp|antigravity-native|unavailable> \
     --browser-observer <auto|playwright-mcp|ego-browser|chrome-devtools-mcp|unavailable> \
     --network-observer <auto|chrome-devtools-mcp|playwright-mcp|ego-browser|unavailable>
   ```
   `run-manifest.mjs` must reject every non-discovery run whose brief is missing, invalid or not `READY`.
   - `browser-driver` and `network-observer` are resolved **independently**; read [references/BROWSER-DRIVER-RESOLUTION.md](references/BROWSER-DRIVER-RESOLUTION.md) for the full flowchart and combination rules
   - `auto` resolves driver priority: `playwright-mcp → ego-browser → chrome-devtools-mcp → antigravity-native → unavailable`
   - `auto` resolves network observer priority: `chrome-devtools-mcp → playwright-mcp → ego-browser → unavailable`
   - ego-browser provides basic network events via `drainEvents()` only (no request/response body); mark network assertions `reduced_confidence` when `network-observer: ego-browser`
   - ego-browser as driver requires macOS; on other platforms resolve to next available driver
   - Prefer `playwright-mcp` network tools when Playwright MCP drives the UI (same session); prefer `chrome-devtools-mcp` network tools only when Chrome DevTools drives or is attached to that exact page
   - Never use an isolated Chrome DevTools browser to claim network evidence for an ego-browser or Playwright session, or the reverse
   - Start observation before the first critical action. After each submit, save, delete, calculation, navigation, upload, retry, permission change, or other business transition, inspect matching XHR/fetch/document requests and console/page errors
   - Inspect response bodies only for failed or contract-relevant requests, including GraphQL HTTP 200 responses with `errors`; redact secrets and personal data before persistence
   - If browser observability is unavailable, mark its ledger row `BLOCKED`. Continue functional testing only when network verification is not part of the requested or business contract
4. With `SHEET_TESTCASE_EXECUTION` (when user provides a Google Sheet URL/ID containing testcases):
   - **Standard schema is pre-baked** — read [references/TESTCASE_SHEET_SCHEMA.json](references/TESTCASE_SHEET_SCHEMA.json); DO NOT rescan headers each time. Schema summary:
     ```
     Sheet: "Test cases_App"  |  Header row: 9 (0-indexed: 8)
     B=Scenario ID  C=Scenario Name  D=Test case ID  E=Description
     F=Pre-condition  G=Procedure  H=Expected Results
     I=Result  J=Priority  K=Date  L=Tester  M=Notes
     ```
     Columns I-M (idx 8-12) are **write columns**; columns B-H (idx 1-7) are **read-only design**.
   - Generate the functional-group worker plan first:
     ```bash
     node scripts/helpers/execute-sheet.mjs \
       --sheet-url <URL> \
       --module <requested-module-if-known> \
       --parallel \
       --plan-only
     ```
   - Read `evidence/sheet/_runs/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<run-id>/sheet-worker-plan.json`, show `Requested module`, exact `Resolved functional groups`, available groups, testcase count and proposed shards, then stop for three explicit user confirmations:
     1. Confirm the exact module/functional-group scope, for example `LOGIN`
     2. Ask how many workers to use from 1 to 4; do not provide a final execution command with a default worker count
     3. Ask whether to run `all`, selected worker IDs such as `1,2`, or `cancel`
   - These confirmations are mandatory in Antigravity and every other host. A module named in the original prompt is a requested filter, not confirmation. Do not silently confirm the module, choose the worker count, or choose all workers
   - Resume with `--module <requested> --confirmed-module <confirmed> --workers <confirmed-count> --selected-workers <all|1,2>`. Missing any confirmation is `BLOCKED` before browser action or write-back
   - When a single module such as `LOGIN` is assigned multiple workers, shard its testcases across the confirmed worker count without duplicating rows; when assignments exceed the concurrency limit, run later waves
   - After the user confirms, delegate each selected assignment to an independent browser sub-agent/worker when the host supports parallel agents
   - Every worker must return JSON matching [references/SHEET_WORKER_RESULT_SCHEMA.json](references/SHEET_WORKER_RESULT_SCHEMA.json). Every `Pass` and `Fail` testcase must include at least one final-state screenshot or video (`png`, `jpg`, `jpeg`, `webp`, `gif`, `mp4`, `webm`, `mov`, `m4v`); JSON, trace, console or network evidence alone is insufficient. `Fail`, `Untest`, and `N/A` require Note
   - Store local media under the assigned `evidence/sheet/<functional-group>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<run-id>/worker-<id>/` or return an `image:`/`video:` remote URL. Store plan, assignments, worker results and write-back JSON separately under `evidence/sheet/_runs/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<run-id>/`. The executor rejects local media outside the testcase's assigned function/date directory and appends valid media references to the Sheet Note
   - Merge worker outputs and import with `--results-file <JSON>`, or supply a real external executor with `--worker-script <PATH>`. Without valid media evidence, no `Pass`/`Fail` cell may be changed
   - **Write-back rules**: `Result` col I: exactly `Pass`, `Fail`, `N/A`, `Untest` (case-sensitive). `Priority` col J: exactly `Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`. `Note` col M: mandatory when Fail/Untest/N/A — concise manual-friendly context (no stacktraces, no raw HTTP codes).
   - After row execution, complete the remaining `SHEET_EXECUTION_PLUS` layers: Sanity, Impacted Regression, Scoped Business Discovery, Exploratory, Ad-hoc, and UI/UX
   - Add Original Retest only for rows tied to a Plane ticket or previously failed execution; do not perform Plane comment/state mutations without a ticket
5. **[BEFORE TEST — VERIFY intelligence provenance]** The preparation command must resolve `<project-root>/qa-knowledge/knowledge-index.json` and current source artifacts before UI execution:
   - If index exists: load only the shard(s) matching the feature/ticket scope — DO NOT load the full guide
   - If index missing: read `app-business-guide.md` as fallback; then read `<feature-slug>-business-guide.md` if it exists
   - Read `permission-matrix.json` (machine-readable, NOT `rbac-matrix.md`) when preparing role-based or security tests
   - Extract and reuse: routes, roles, state transitions, validation rules, API contracts, side effects, reusable assets, source file/line and confidence
   - If guide is older than current sprint or environment has changed: flag fields as `unresolved` and re-verify during test
   - If NO guide exists at all: run scoped discovery for a retest; use `APP_BASELINE_DISCOVERY` only for an explicit full-app/bootstrap request
6. With `RETEST_TICKET` -> read ticket via `plane-qa`, record scoped Business Discovery as the shared foundation, then create the mandatory RETEST_PLUS ledger with all 6 items: **Retest, Sanity, Impacted regression, Exploratory, Ad-hoc, UI/UX**. Full workflow: [references/RETEST-PLUS.md](references/RETEST-PLUS.md).
7. Copy the test contract from the `READY` brief. Do not rewrite it from memory or replace missing fields with generic steps.
8. Run CLI/scripts for clear and repetitive flows; only use browser agent/MCP for interactive branches not yet understood.
9. Update verdict/evidence into the ledger immediately after each layer; do not conclude if any item lacks a verdict or `BLOCKED/PARTIAL` reason.
10. Separate the original ticket verdict from new bugs, then apply the fixed state map via `plane-qa`.
11. After every run, run `node scripts/analysis/finding-reconciler.mjs --findings evidence/<run-res>.json --permission-matrix <pm.json>` to close the feedback loop, bundle evidence via `scripts/helpers/collect-evidence.mjs`, and finalize via `scripts/helpers/run-manifest.mjs finish <RUN_ID>`.
12. **[AFTER EVERY RUN — WRITE knowledge]** Update the business guide before closing the session — this is mandatory, not optional:
    ```bash
    # Step 1: write/merge the knowledge update
    node scripts/writers/write-business-guide.mjs guide-update.json <project-root>
    # Step 2: validate the written guide reads back correctly
    node scripts/writers/write-business-guide.mjs --check <project-root>/qa-knowledge/<feature-slug>-business-guide.md
    ```
    Minimum facts to record after each run:
    - Confirmed happy flow steps (with routes and roles)
    - Business rules verified or disproved
    - State transitions observed
    - API/network contracts confirmed
    - Known issues found (new or persistent)
    - Reusable assets (locators, data setups, routes, test accounts)
    - `latest_run` block: scope, verdict, key notes
    - Mark any previously `inferred` facts as `verified` if run confirmed them
    If guide already exists: set `previous_guide` path and `merge_confirmed: true` in JSON update; do not delete any fact the current run did not touch

State map: `PASS → Done`, `FAILED → In Progress`, `BLOCKED → unchanged`, `new bug → Todo`

## Knowledge scope decision

- `APP_BASELINE_DISCOVERY`: bootstrap project lacking `qa-knowledge/knowledge-index.json`. Run `scripts/helpers/extract-flow.mjs` first; map modules → traverse accessible main business flows, role/state/input/side-effect/integration/UI/UX and coverage gaps.
- `REPO_BUSINESS_DISCOVERY`: run `node scripts/orchestrators/repo-business-discovery.mjs --repo <path> --mode <full|incremental> --graphify auto`. Graphify runs code-only when available and contributes dependency candidates; canonical QA-skill scanners still produce rules, flows, contracts and permissions. Use `--graphify required` only when Graphify itself is required by the user
- `SHEET_TESTCASE_EXECUTION`: load `qa-knowledge/app-flow-map.json`, generate the plan with `node scripts/helpers/execute-sheet.mjs --sheet-url <URL> --module <requested-if-known> --parallel --plan-only`, show the resolved module scope, then ask the user to confirm module, worker count 1-4 and worker selection. Run only confirmed assignments and import image/video-backed results. Finish every `SHEET_EXECUTION_PLUS` layer
- `RETEST_TICKET`: do not rescan the full app. Run Scoped Business Discovery from ticket/index shards, refresh only missing or stale feature knowledge, then finish every RETEST_PLUS row.
- `SANITY_REGRESSION` and `EXPLORATORY_ADHOC`: reuse existing guides, expand `DISCOVERY_CORE`, and update knowledge exactly in the inspected scope.
- Do not call baseline exhaustive if you have not traversed enough modules, roles, states or data. Log `covered`, `partial`, `blocked` or `not_covered` in `coverage_map`.

## Critical red flags (hard stop)

These must be observed at all times, even before reading any reference file:

- **DO NOT run destructive tests** (delete, drop, wipe data) without explicit user authorization
- **DO NOT skip any hard gate** — all gates above are mandatory regardless of context or time pressure
- **DO NOT conclude PASS when lacking evidence** — absence of visible error is not evidence of passing
- **DO NOT use fallback (Antigravity/CLI) as a substitute for MCP** without first confirming MCP is genuinely unavailable
- **DO NOT overwrite existing artifacts** (`auth.json`, `evidence/`, `qa-knowledge/`) without reading the existing content first
- **DO NOT mix browser sessions** — network and console evidence must come from the same page/session that executed the UI action
- **DO NOT treat every 4xx/5xx as a confirmed bug** — correlate the request with the triggering action, expected negative behavior, response body and visible outcome
- **DO NOT replace business-risk exploration with a generic element checklist** — derive charters from requirement, knowledge, source and runtime signals
- **DO NOT call a static source claim runtime-verified** — preserve provenance and reconcile contradictions explicitly
- **DO NOT treat Graphify output as a business rule, expected result or coverage proof** — keep every relation `source-derived-candidate` and preserve `EXTRACTED`, `INFERRED` or `AMBIGUOUS`
- **DO NOT confuse the bounded `contextSlice` or HTML overview canvas with project completeness** — retain all normalized nodes/relations by default and retrieve only the relevant slice into AI context
- **DO NOT let an optional HTML companion replace canonical JSON, Markdown, Excel or XMind** — render only after the source artifact validates

## Canonical artifact layout

```text
<project-root>/
├── .env
├── auth.json
├── evidence/
│   ├── runs/<run-id>/ (manifest.json, screenshots/, logs/, redacted/)
│   ├── network/<run-id>/ (sanitized request/response summaries)
│   ├── console/<run-id>/ (sanitized error/warning summaries)
│   ├── sheet/<functional-group>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<run-id>/worker-<id>/ (Sheet screenshots/videos)
│   ├── sheet/_runs/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<run-id>/ (Sheet plans/results/write-back metadata)
│   ├── visual-*/
│   └── .runtime-events.json
├── qa-knowledge/
│   ├── knowledge-index.json        ← entry point (always read first)
│   ├── system-overview.md
│   ├── flows/, rules/, contracts/, evidence/
│   ├── app-business-guide.md       ← compatibility/overview layer
│   ├── app-flow-map.json
│   ├── checklists/, merged/, repositories/, ui-business/
│   ├── repositories/<repo>/graphify-discovery.json
│   ├── repositories/<repo>/graphify-code-only/graphify-out/
├── FINDINGS.md
└── reports/ (retest/, exports/)
```

## Output format

- Plane comments and testcase prose must have no `.` at end of sentence and no emojis/icons
- Preserve ID, URL, filename, formula, code, decimal number and machine-readable values
- PASS comment: Result + Conclusion + inline image only
- FAILED comment: adds Actual + Expected
- BLOCKED comment: adds Blocker only

# Test Case Template

**Core principle:** Same set of columns — do not invent new columns.

Original template: `assets/Template.xlsx` (1 shared file for ALL projects). All project information (name, code, modules) is configurable from JSON input. **NO need to create separate templates per project**.

> **When to use**: User wants to write Excel test cases according to team standards.
> **DIFFERENT** from `qa-run` (live exploratory) and `playwright-pom-automation` (code automation `.spec.ts`): this skill = document Excel test cases (manual test design).
> **API key**: shared from `../config/api_keys.json` (see scripts/ai_provider.py) — NO key needed if using Copilot Pro/Antigravity/Claude Code CLI. Members can run immediately with any project after git clone.

## Cross-model hard gates

Apply this exact order for all models:

1. Choose mode before writing: default to current UI/FUNCTION flow; only use API mode when user explicitly requests writing API testcases or writing testcases for endpoints, OpenAPI/Swagger, Postman or curl; merely mentioning API artifacts is not enough to switch modes
2. If API mode has source files, run `scripts/import-api-spec.py` first; do not manually read and copy endpoints
3. Check `review_required`; if items remain, stop Excel generation and get missing expected from user or documents
4. Read requirement/AC and list requirement IDs before writing cases
5. Choose UI or FUNCTION correctly based on the behavior to prove; do not call a case UI-only just because it operates via dialog/button
6. Split scenario when field, behavior or AC differs; one scenario contains only one specific functional group
7. Create JSON with correct schema, preserve Scenario ID, Testcase ID and requirement reference
8. Run `scripts/gen-testcases.py`; script must create `<output>.md` before `<output>.xlsx` with the same `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` date
9. Read Markdown first then compare with Excel: number of cases, Scenario/Testcase ID and design content must match; columns I-M exist only in Excel and are left blank

If expected is not in requirements, pause that case in a clarification state; do not fabricate business rules.

## The trap this skill exists to prevent

**Freeform columns per author** — each tester invents their own column set, breaking cross-project aggregation and review tooling. Skill enforces a single shared template so test cases from different projects can be queried, compared, and rolled up.

## Process

### 1. Read & extract requirements
**MANDATORY to stick to documents**. Every case must trace to 1 AC. If NO document -> ask user. Plane fetch details: `@references/plane-integration.md`.

### 2. Organize in 2 parts + type order
```
PHẦN 1 — UI: 1.1. USER INTERFACE (kind=ui)    ← col C, xanh nhạt
└─ Group (LOGIN, REGISTER...)                 ← col C, group header
   └─ Scenario (SCN-LOG-001)                  ← col B
      └─ Cases — type order

PHẦN 2 — FUNCTIONAL: 1.2. FUNCTION (kind=function) ← col C, xanh lá
└─ Group (LOGIN, REGISTER...)
   └─ Scenario (SCN-LOG-001)
      └─ Cases — type order
```
**Same feature can exist in both parts** (UI test for display, Functional test for logic). For UI testcases (`kind=ui`), you MUST read [references/ui-testcases.md](references/ui-testcases.md) to follow the UI testing checklist.

**API mode is optional**: only when user requests API testcases, read [references/api-testcases.md](references/api-testcases.md). API cases still go in `1.2. FUNCTION`, use `kind=api` and keep columns B-M. If user does not request API, do not read this reference and continue current flow with `kind=ui` or `kind=function`.

**Rule: 1 scenario = 1 specific functional group** (DO NOT group multiple fields/behaviors):
- Split scenario when **field/input** differs (email validation != password validation -> 2 scenarios)
- Split scenario when **behavior** differs (submit-fail != account-lock)
- Split scenario when **AC** differs (AC3 != AC4 != AC5)
- Same `scenario_name` SHARED across cases IN THE SAME scenario — but DO NOT share scenario_name for validations of different fields

WRONG vs CORRECT examples for login page:
```
❌ WRONG: 1 scenario \"Validation email and password\" groups 6 cases
       (3 cases email validation + 2 cases password validation + 1 case both empty)
       -> Hard for tester to filter, hard to check coverage, ambiguous scenario_name

✅ CORRECT: split 2 separate scenarios
   - SCN-LOG-002 \"Validation email\"        -> email cases (empty, missing @, missing domain, subdomain)
   - SCN-LOG-003 \"Validation password\"     -> password cases (empty, both empty, <8 chars, =8 chars)
   -> Each scenario has 1 clear group, tester can filter, coverage easy to check
```

### 3. Gen cases by type order

**Before writing any case, identify the BB technique:**

- `happy` / `alternative` → Use Case Testing
- `validation` → EP + BVA; if ≥2 combined conditions → **build Decision Table first**
- `edge` → BVA: list min−1, min, min+1, max−1, max, max+1 before writing
- `negative` → EP (invalid partition) + Error Guessing checklist
- `error` → Error Guessing + State Transition
- `additional` → Error Guessing; always flag `Ref: (out-of-spec)`

8 types: `happy → alternative → validation → edge → negative → error → ui → additional`. Full technique guide + JSON examples: `@references/blackbox-techniques.md`.

### 4. Build JSON input
```json
{
  "project": {"code": "BCP", "name": "BCP AI", ...},
  "scenarios": [{
    "scenario_id": "SCN-LOG-001",
    "requirement": "AC1",
    "scenario_name": "Đăng nhập thành công",
    "cases": [{
      "type": "happy", "req": "AC1",
      "description": "Xác minh rằng người dùng có thể đăng nhập với email + password đúng",
      "pre_condition": "Có account test",
      "procedure": "1. Mở /login\n2. Nhập email + password\n3. Click nút Login",
      "expected": "1. Đăng nhập thành công",
      "priority": "High"
    }]
  }]
}
```
- `scenario_name` (string) — functional group name, **SHARED** for multiple cases in same scenario
- `scenario_id` (string) — scenario code, e.g. `SCN-LOG-001`
- Each case has `type` (1 of 8) + `req` (trace to AC) - MANDATORY
- In API mode specifically, each case adds `api` object; see [examples/sample-api-input.json](examples/sample-api-input.json). Without `api` object, generator uses `pre_condition`, `procedure`, `expected` as is

### 5. Run gen script

If user requests API testcases from source file/folder, import first:

```bash
python3 scripts/import-api-spec.py api-file output-api.json \
  --project-code CODE --project-name "Project Name"
```

Only run Excel step when command returns exit code `0` and `review_required` is empty. For endpoints/curls without declared response status, user can confirm and pass `--default-success-status 200`; do not auto-add this option without confirmation.

```bash
python3 scripts/gen-testcases.py input.json OneBrain_Testcases.xlsx
```
-> Script auto-generates `OneBrain_Testcases_<DD-MM-YYYY>.md` first -> copies template -> updates Cover from JSON -> cleanups -> writes section/group/case rows -> hardcodes matching Testcase IDs -> saves `OneBrain_Testcases_<DD-MM-YYYY>.xlsx`.

### Artifact filename date

- Append the `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` creation date immediately before the extension as `_DD-MM-YYYY`, for example `OneBrain_Testcases_20-07-2026.xlsx`
- Use the same date for the Markdown and Excel companions
- Do not append a second date when the requested basename already ends in `_DD-MM-YYYY`
- Do not rename existing artifacts
- When the user supplies an exact filename that must remain unchanged, set `QA_PRESERVE_EXACT_FILENAME=1` for the generator

Markdown is the AI-readable version to understand testcases without parsing Excel. Read [references/markdown-testcases.md](references/markdown-testcases.md) and do not edit the two files independently.

In API mode, generator only maps the `api` object to F/G/H. Regular testcases lack the `api` object so it keeps the current execution path and row height settings.

### Output cleanup (auto)

Original template `assets/Template.xlsx` intentionally keeps **many sample group headers** (REGISTER, LOGIN, HOME, BOOKING, PROFILE, SETTING, NOTIFICATION, DASHBOARD) as reference for AI to know structure + row padding from Excel. When generating output, script automatically:

1. **Dynamic whitelist**: only keep group headers declared in `JSON sections[].groups[].name`. Unused sample groups -> deleted completely.
2. **Dynamic group**: auto-creates groups/tags not already in template and allocates enough rows for all cases
3. **Delete rows**: any remaining empty rows (skipped groups + sample case rows) -> completely deleted via `ws.delete_rows()`, not keeping fill color / row height.
4. **Sequential numbering**: `[CODE-UI-NN]` for UI (1-4), `[CODE-NN]` for Functional (5-30) in the same file.

**Result**: output file is compact, containing only actual data for current project (e.g. demo project with 1 LOGIN group x 2 sections -> file ~43 rows instead of 657 template rows).

### Column schema (Test cases_App sheet)

| Col | Fill | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| B | Scenario ID | e.g. `SCN-LOG-001` |
| C | **Scenario Name** (shared) | Feature group name, not the test case name |
| D | **Test case ID** (hardcoded) | `[CODE-NN]` (Functional) or `[CODE-UI-NN]` (UI). Sequential. |
| E | **Description** (manual) | Start with "Verify that...", NO technical prefix |
| F | Pre-condition | State/data required before step 1 |
| G | Procedure | Numbered steps `1. ...\n2. ...` — manual language, detailed enough to execute without interpretation |
| H | Expected Results | Observable, measurable outcome |
| I-M | **LEAVE BLANK** | Tester fills during execution |

**Important**: Columns I-M are left empty by the generator. Script applies style only — no value fill. Testers fill these when running actual tests.

### Manual-Friendly Writing Rules (MANDATORY for every case)

> **Invariant rule**: Every testcase in this system is written for a **Manual Tester who reads the Excel sheet and executes immediately** — not for developers or API tools.

> **Language rule**: Rule files and skill instructions are written in English for faster AI parsing. However, ALL testcase content written into Excel/Markdown (Description, Pre-condition, Procedure, Expected Results) MUST be in **Vietnamese**, as Testers read and execute from those files.

**1. Description — Use end-user language, written in Vietnamese:**
- ✅ CORRECT: *Xác minh rằng người dùng không thể đăng nhập khi để trống ô Mật khẩu*
- ❌ WRONG: *Verify POST /auth/login returns 400 when password=null*
- ❌ WRONG: *[TC-03][negative] Empty password validation*

**2. Procedure / Steps — Detailed enough for anyone to follow without interpretation:**

Each step must specify: **What to do** + **Where** + **Exact value/content** (if applicable). Never combine multiple actions into one line.

- ✅ CORRECT (Vietnamese content):
  ```
  1. Mở trình duyệt và truy cập trang đăng nhập: [URL]/login
  2. Tại ô "Email", nhập email hợp lệ: test@example.com
  3. Tại ô "Mật khẩu", để trống (không nhập gì)
  4. Nhấp vào nút "Đăng nhập"
  5. Quan sát kết quả hiển thị trên màn hình
  ```
- ❌ WRONG: *Nhập email hợp lệ và để trống mật khẩu, click login*
- ❌ WRONG: *Send request with empty password field*

**3. Expected Results — Observable, measurable, visible to the eye:**

Describe exactly what the Tester sees or can verify after performing the steps. Avoid vague language.

- ✅ CORRECT (Vietnamese content):
  ```
  1. Hệ thống không thực hiện đăng nhập
  2. Dưới ô "Mật khẩu" hiển thị thông báo màu đỏ: "Mật khẩu không được để trống"
  3. Trang không chuyển hướng, vẫn ở màn hình đăng nhập
  ```
- ❌ WRONG: *Hệ thống xử lý đúng*
- ❌ WRONG: *Response body: {"error": "password required"}*

**4. Forbidden technical language in columns F, G, H (write in Vietnamese instead):**

| Instead of this ❌ | Write this ✅ (Vietnamese) |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/login` | Nhấp nút "Đăng nhập" |
| `HTTP 400 Bad Request` | Hiển thị thông báo lỗi |
| `response.body.token` | Hệ thống cấp quyền truy cập |
| `null`, `undefined`, `NaN` | Để trống, không nhập gì |
| `assert status == 200` | Kiểm tra trang chuyển hướng về Dashboard |

### Human-readable format

- No trailing `.` at the end of Scenario Name, Description, Pre-condition, Procedure, or Expected Results
- No emoji/icons in testcase content
- Keep Scenario ID, Testcase ID, requirement ID, URL, filename, formula, code, and decimal numbers unchanged
- New Markdown and Excel filenames must share the same basename with suffix `_DD-MM-YYYY`
- Generator auto-validates icons and strips trailing dots from prose

### Template structure details

See `@references/template-schema.md` for details on the 4 sheets (Cover, Test cases_App, Dropdown Keys, Report).

## Black-Box Techniques

Mọi case phải dùng it́ nhát 1 kĩ thuạt BB. Xác định khi làm buước 3, ghi vào `bb_technique` để trace (generator bỏ qua, không ảnh huưởng Excel).

| Kĩ thuạt | Type áp dụng | Khi nào bát buọc |
|---|---|---|
| **Equivalence Partitioning (EP)** | `validation`, `negative` | Luôn áp dụng khi có input partition |
| **Boundary Value Analysis (BVA)** | `edge`, `validation` | Khi field có giới hạn số, độ dài, ngày |
| **Decision Table** | `validation`, `negative`, `happy` | Bắt buộc khi ≥2 điều kiện kết hợp |
| **State Transition** | `happy`, `alternative`, `error`, `negative` | Khi object có ≥2 trạng thái rõ ràng |
| **Use Case Testing** | `happy`, `alternative`, `ui` | Mặc định cho flow AC |
| **Error Guessing** | `negative`, `error`, `additional` | Luôn áp dụng sau các kỹ thuật khác |
| **Pairwise** | `validation`, `edge` | Khi ≥3 input field độc lập |

**Decision rule:**

```
≥2 điều kiện kết hợp?  → Decision Table bắt buộc trước
Có giá trị biên (độ dài, số, ngày)?  → BVA bắt buộc cho edge
Có ≥2 traạng thái?  → Veẽ state diagram trướng
Có ≥3 field đọc lạp?  → Dùng Pairwise thay full factorial
Còn lại?  → Use Case Testing + EP + Error Guessing
```

Xem hướng dẫn đầy đủ + JSON mẫu: [`references/blackbox-techniques.md`](references/blackbox-techniques.md)

## Red flags

| Symptom | Why it's wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Output file > 200 rows for a small project | Sample rows from template not deleted | Verify dynamic whitelist in JSON includes all required groups |
| Non-sequential test case IDs (`[BCP-01]`, `[BCP-03]` missing `[BCP-02]`) | STT offset when type order changes | Re-run script; ensure correct 8-type canonical order |
| Columns I-M pre-filled with data | Script applied value fill instead of style only | Verify `gen-testcases.py` branch applies style only, no value fill |
| Description starts with `[STT]` or `[Type]` | Manual format violated | AI must reformat before writing to JSON |
| Procedure is a single line combining multiple actions | Tester cannot identify where to act | Split each action into its own numbered step; include field/button name and input value |
| Procedure or Expected uses technical terms (`POST`, `HTTP 400`, `null`, `assert`) | Not manual-tester language | Replace with UI descriptions the tester sees (button names, displayed messages) |
| Expected result is vague ("system works correctly", "error handled") | Not measurable; tester does not know what to check | State the exact message shown, the page redirected to, or data displayed |
| Expected result contains JSON body or HTTP status code | Written as an API test; tester cannot verify visually | Replace with what the user sees on the UI |
| New columns added (Method/Endpoint/Status) | Breaks fixed template format | Put API data into F/G/H per the API reference |
| API mode auto-enabled for regular testcases | Changes current configuration | Only enable when user explicitly requests API testcases |
| API case only checks status code | Missing contract and business effect | Also verify body/schema/headers/side-effects when requirement defines them |
| Real token, cookie, or API key written into workbook | Credential leak into artifact | Use placeholder like `<valid_token>` |
| Status 200 assumed for endpoint with no response contract | Fabricated expected result | Let importer set `review_required` then ask user or read docs |
| Swagger read manually with missed endpoints | Non-deterministic; weak models make mistakes | Always run `scripts/import-api-spec.py` |
| Only Excel created, no Markdown testcase companion | AI must parse workbook next time | Always use generator to create Markdown before Excel |
| Markdown and Excel content diverge | Two artifacts edited independently | Fix JSON source then regenerate both |

## Common mistakes

- **Every case MUST have `req` pointing to one AC** (Notes: `Ref: ACx`). No ref → case cannot be traced, fails coverage check.

- **Grouping different fields/behaviors into one scenario** — e.g. one scenario "Email and password validation" combining both. WRONG. Must split into two: "Email validation" and "Password validation". See Process step 2 for split criteria.

- **`additional` cases (outside spec)** → flag clearly with `Ref: (out-of-spec)` and notify user. Do not ship as a normal case.

- **NEVER fabricate expected results** from vague spec — ask user. Spec says "handle error gracefully" → DO NOT self-define what "gracefully" means.

- **Description format MANUAL**: "Verify that..." — no `[STT]`, `[Type]`, stray `/`. This format lets testers reading the Excel understand immediately.

- **Multiple cases in the SAME scenario may share `scenario_name`** (shared feature group name). Don't duplicate names per case. BUT do not merge cases of different fields/behaviors — split them (see Process step 2).

- **When cloning to a new machine**: run `pip install openpyxl PyYAML` first. `PyYAML` is required for Swagger/OpenAPI YAML. API key configured once in `config/api_keys.json` (gitignored) — shared across all 3 skills.

- **Key configuration**: one shared config file `../config/api_keys.json` (gitignored), usable by all 3 skills. See [README.md](../README.md) section "API Keys".

# Whitebox QA

Use the local AST CLI as the parser. Use AI only to select scope, reconcile requirements, create explicit mappings, and interpret verified output.

## Hard gates

1. Resolve an exact repository and named function or method
2. Run `find` when file or class is unknown
3. Stop on multiple matches; require exact `--file` and optionally `--class`
4. Keep `sourceHash`, language, parser, branch IDs, path IDs, limits, and warnings with every result
5. Label static output and every generated candidate `source-derived-candidate`
6. Say `covered`, `uncovered`, or report a percentage only after a runtime report is imported
   Before import, preserve the exact state `No runtime coverage evidence supplied`
7. Do not modify application source unless the user separately requests implementation
8. Generate Jest/Vitest only from an explicit mapping with executable body lines; never emit `TODO` tests
9. Do not create a testcase workbook directly; use [testcase handoff](references/testcase-handoff.md)
10. Stop testcase document generation when expected behavior or requirement mapping is unresolved

## Runtime doctor

From this skill directory:

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npm run test:coverage
npm run benchmark
```

Node.js 20 or newer is required. MCP is not required. Report missing dependencies as `runtime_missing` and build failures with the exact compiler error.

## Resolve and analyze

Find every exact match:

```bash
npm run cli -- find processPayment --repo /absolute/repository
```

Analyze one resolved target:

```bash
npm run cli -- analyze \
  --repo /absolute/repository \
  --file src/payment/payment.service.ts \
  --class PaymentService \
  --function processPayment
```

The default is compact JSON to limit context usage. Use full JSON only for test generation, runtime coverage, or testcase handoff:

```bash
npm run cli -- analyze \
  --repo /absolute/repository \
  --file src/payment/payment.service.ts \
  --class PaymentService \
  --function processPayment \
  --format json \
  --output /absolute/repository/reports/process-payment
```

Read [analysis schema](references/analysis-schema.md) before interpreting full output and [token budget](references/token-budget.md) before expanding repository scope.

## Build a bounded call graph

```bash
npm run cli -- graph \
  --repo /absolute/repository \
  --file src/payment/payment.service.ts \
  --class PaymentService \
  --function processPayment \
  --max-depth 5 \
  --max-nodes 100
```

The graph works for every supported language. Resolved edges may be traversed; ambiguous, external, reflective, or dynamic calls remain explicit unresolved edges. Read [graphs and NestJS](references/graphs-and-nestjs.md).

For NestJS module, controller, route, provider, and constructor-DI extraction:

```bash
npm run cli -- nestjs \
  --repo /absolute/repository \
  --output /absolute/repository/reports/nestjs-graph.json
```

For a large, cross-language or unfamiliar repository, use the optional Graphify adapter only to select the exact bounded scope:

```bash
node ../qa-run/scripts/discovery/graphify-adapter.mjs --doctor
node ../qa-run/scripts/discovery/graphify-adapter.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/repository \
  --output /absolute/repository/reports/graphify-discovery.json \
  --mode auto
```

Read [Graphify and effective HTML integration](../qa-run/references/GRAPHIFY-EFFECTIVE-HTML.md) before using this layer. Preserve every Graphify relation as `source-derived-candidate`. Then run the local `whitebox graph` command for the named function; Graphify never replaces exact function resolution, branch/path analysis or coverage import

Render an optional interactive companion only after the graph JSON validates:

```bash
node ../qa-run/scripts/writers/render-intelligence-html.mjs \
  --input reports/process-payment-call-graph.json \
  --output reports/process-payment-call-graph.html

node ../qa-run/scripts/writers/render-intelligence-html.mjs \
  --check reports/process-payment-call-graph.html
```

The HTML is a derived view and cannot change evidence level

## Generate executable Jest or Vitest

Analyze with `--format json`, then create an explicit unit-test mapping:

```bash
npm run cli -- generate-test \
  --analysis reports/process-payment.json \
  --mapping reports/process-payment.unit-test-mapping.json \
  --output tests/process-payment.whitebox.test.ts
```

The generated file contains real imports, setup, hooks, assertions supplied by the mapping, and trace comments for candidate/path/branch IDs. The command rejects unknown or duplicate candidate IDs. Read [unit tests and runtime coverage](references/unit-tests-and-coverage.md).

## Run and import runtime coverage

Run the local project binary without invoking a shell:

```bash
npm run cli -- run-coverage \
  --runner vitest \
  --cwd /absolute/repository \
  --analysis reports/process-payment.json \
  --test tests/process-payment.whitebox.test.ts \
  --output reports/process-payment.runtime.json
```

Use `--runner jest` for Jest and `--config <path>` when the repository requires an explicit config. The command fails when tests fail, the local runner is missing, or `coverage-final.json` is absent.

If tests were run separately, import an existing Istanbul report:

```bash
npm run cli -- coverage \
  --analysis reports/process-payment.json \
  --report coverage/coverage-final.json \
  --output reports/process-payment.runtime.json
```

Runtime evidence changes each candidate's `runtimeCoverage` to `covered`, `partial`, `uncovered`, or `unknown`. The approval state remains `source-derived-candidate` until business expectations are confirmed.

## Generate testcase documents

Use the existing template generator only:

```bash
npm run cli -- handoff \
  --analysis reports/process-payment.runtime.json \
  --mapping reports/process-payment.mapping.json \
  --output-json reports/process-payment.testcases.json \
  --xlsx reports/process-payment-testcases.xlsx
```

The handoff validates explicit AC or `(out-of-spec)` mappings, creates canonical `testcase-template` JSON, and invokes `testcase-template/scripts/gen-testcases.py` to generate Markdown before Excel.

## Supported scope

| Language | Files | Parser |
|---|---|---|
| TypeScript | `.ts`, `.tsx` | ts-morph |
| JavaScript | `.js`, `.jsx` | ts-morph |
| Python | `.py` | ast-grep/tree-sitter |
| Java | `.java` | ast-grep/tree-sitter |
| Go | `.go` | ast-grep/tree-sitter |
| C# | `.cs` | ast-grep/tree-sitter |
| Dart | `.dart` | ast-grep/tree-sitter |

Static adapters normalize functions/methods, `if/else`, switch or match cases, `try/catch/finally`, loops, return, throw, path limits, and cyclomatic estimates. Read [language adapters](references/language-adapters.md) for language-specific behavior.

## Evidence levels

1. Static AST result: source-derived possibility
2. Generated executable test: code artifact, not proof it passed
3. Passing Jest/Vitest run: execution evidence for that run
4. Imported coverage counts: measured branch/statement evidence for the matching target revision
5. Requirement-mapped testcase: approved business expectation only after requirement review

Never collapse these levels into one claim.

## Known limits

- Compound boolean expressions are one decision unless their AST contains nested control-flow statements
- Call graphs are bounded and best-effort; reflection, runtime registration, generated code, interface dispatch, and external libraries can remain unresolved
- NestJS resolution covers decorators, module arrays, imports, constructor types, and `@Inject` tokens visible in source; custom provider factories and runtime tokens may remain unresolved
- Automatic runtime execution currently supports local Jest/Vitest with Istanbul JSON; other language runners need a compatible adapter or externally produced evidence
- Static reachability is not runtime proof, even when a path looks complete
- Repository-wide Graphify relations are supplemental candidates and may not expand a bounded function graph without exact local resolution
